title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; previous bounds like Landauer's are limited to erasure, but general computation requires more general thermodynamic constraints.
method: Applies stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation-dissipation theorems to derive trade-offs between work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing systems.
result: Establishes optimal computation from fluctuation responses, providing tight bounds on energy dissipation for arbitrary logical operations.
conclusion: The results unify thermodynamics and computation, showing that optimal computation is governed by fluctuation-response relations, with implications for designing energy-efficient computing.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, achieving coherent control and readout of the nuclear spin qubit.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times and high control fidelities, but existing platforms rely on donor atoms. This work explores an alternative using 73Ge nuclear spins in a quantum dot, which may offer advantages in scalability and integration with silicon quantum dot qubits.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon quantum dot device with a natural abundance of 73Ge isotopes. They use electrical spin resonance techniques to coherently drive the nuclear spin and read out its state via the quantum dot charge sensor.
result: They demonstrate coherent Rabi oscillations and Ramsey fringes of the 73Ge nuclear spin, extract coherence times (T2* ~ 10 μs, T2 ~ 100 μs), and show single-shot readout fidelity above 90%.
conclusion: This work establishes 73Ge nuclear spins in silicon quantum dots as a viable qubit platform, combining the long coherence of nuclear spins with the scalability of quantum dot technology.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale machines and biological oscillators.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating the entropy production rate to the coherence number of the oscillation.
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and provide a rigorous proof that the entropy produced per period is at least proportional to the logarithm of the coherence number.
conclusion: The tradeoff sets a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the precision of autonomous oscillations, with implications for biochemical clocks and quantum heat engines.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series data using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic properties from experimental time-series data is challenging; the authors aim to extract thermodynamic quantities without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: They introduce a framework based on correlation currents and trajectory-fluctuation currents, leveraging machine learning to learn the underlying stochastic thermodynamics from observed trajectories.
result: The method successfully reconstructs thermodynamic forces, entropy production, and other key quantities from simulated and experimental data, demonstrating accuracy and robustness.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for inferring thermodynamics in complex systems where direct measurement of forces or entropy production is infeasible.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling for long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with a focus on entanglement swapping and measurement-device-independent techniques to extend distance.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical secure quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: This work provides a consistent thermodynamic description for quantum systems with limited measurement access, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory; this work aims to demonstrate that time can be defined internally via entropy exchange.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different sectors (e.g., motional and internal degrees of freedom) is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, showing that time can be emergent from thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The experiment provides a concrete realization of time as an emergent concept from thermodynamics, supporting the idea that time may not be fundamental but arises from entropy exchange.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors model a satellite-to-ground link with realistic parameters (atmospheric turbulence, detector noise, etc.) and simulate the performance of decoy-state BB84 at GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, achieving secure key rates of several Mbps over typical LEO passes.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD is a promising route to practical global quantum communication networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity dissipation into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including spin-squeezed and topological states.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, and demonstrate its application to ultraprecise sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws for information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and communication; previous work showed that measurements can induce transitions in entanglement scaling, but the lifetime of quantum information under monitoring was not well understood.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the dynamics of quantum information through quantities like mutual information and entanglement entropy, and derive scaling laws using analytical arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with the system size in the volume-law phase, and polynomially in the area-law phase, with a crossover at the measurement-induced phase transition.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a strategy for error mitigation in near-term quantum devices.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanical mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to different decoding phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and have implications for quantum error correction and information thermodynamics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to loss. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical repeater architectures.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage. Performance is evaluated through numerical simulations of entanglement distribution rates.
result: The optimized tree codes achieve higher entanglement distribution rates with fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer emitters and lower memory requirements) compared to symmetric codes, and are more robust to photon loss.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for quantum information processing, overcoming limitations of existing systems.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for spin qubits and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios; incorporating realistic device characterization can improve key rates and enable certification.
method: The authors develop a modular framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) into entropy accumulation theorem-based security proofs, maintaining composable security.
result: The method yields tighter finite-key bounds and a systematic way to translate experimental characterizations into security parameters.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, enabling rigorous security certification of QKD systems with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are promising for quantum computing, but scaling to many atoms is limited by serial addressing. This work aims to parallelize operations using multiple cavity modes.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple transverse cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms in a 2D array, leveraging spatial mode multiplexing and cavity quantum electrodynamics.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations, significantly reducing the time required for multi-qubit gates and state readout compared to serial approaches.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral-atom arrays, combining the advantages of cavity enhancement and parallel processing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout on the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubit performance.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They identify a sharp transition between decodable and nondecodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties show universal behavior near the transition.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for such hybrid processors.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations, defining hybrid stabilizer states and codes.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes, and show that these codes can improve displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a foundation for quantum error correction and sensing in hybrid systems, bridging discrete and continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground state is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose fundamental constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is essential for advancing quantum thermodynamics and quantum control.
method: The authors derive rigorous bounds on cooling using Gaussian operations via covariance matrix analysis and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can achieve lower temperatures, using both analytical and numerical methods.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited by the initial squeezing and thermal occupation, but non-Gaussian resources provide a systematic enhancement, enabling sub-bath temperatures beyond Gaussian reach.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations are a powerful resource for bosonic cooling, with implications for quantum heat engines, quantum memories, and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the impact of Markovian noise on quantum memories is crucial for practical quantum information processing, yet the fundamental limits of storage and error correction under such noise were not fully characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum information theory, including entropy measures and channel capacities, to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory. They derive bounds on storage fidelity and error correction thresholds.
result: The paper derives tight bounds on the maximum achievable storage fidelity and the minimum required resources for error correction under Markovian noise, revealing a trade-off between memory lifetime and error correction overhead.
conclusion: Markovian noise imposes fundamental constraints on quantum memory performance, and the derived bounds provide guidelines for designing optimal error correction strategies.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale to macroscopic deterministic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems that preserves thermodynamic laws at macroscopic scales, challenging traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles from Markov jump processes, applied to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in macroscopic systems far from equilibrium.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, linking mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to macroscopic laws.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is shown to be more noise-tolerant than previous methods, and is demonstrated experimentally with a four-qubit entangled state.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, advancing both fundamental tests and quantum network applications.

title: Entanglement Improving Coordination In Distributed Systems
authors: Francisco Ferreira Da Silva And Stephanie Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Ferreira da Silva and Stephanie Wehner

Coordination in distributed systems is often hampered by communication latency, which degrades performance. Quantum entanglement offers fundamentally stronger correlations than classically achievable without communication. Crucially, these correlations manifest instantaneously upon measurement, irre…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062611] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement can improve coordination in distributed systems by reducing the impact of communication latency.
motivation: Coordination in distributed systems is limited by communication latency; quantum entanglement offers stronger-than-classical correlations that could mitigate this.
method: The authors analyze a distributed coordination task and prove that entanglement provides an advantage over classical resources, using information-theoretic tools.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement enables better coordination than any classical strategy without communication, and quantify the advantage.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement is a valuable resource for distributed coordination, with implications for quantum networks and distributed quantum computing.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
authors: Robin Krebs And Mariami Gachechiladze
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to scale bound entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems using local extensions, providing new insights into the structure of entanglement.
motivation: Understanding the structure of entanglement in high dimensions is crucial for quantum information processing, but it remains poorly characterized. The authors aim to generalize peel-off theorems to bound entangled states.
method: The authors introduce a technique called 'local extensions' that allows them to relate the entanglement of a high-dimensional state to that of its lower-dimensional substates, proving a scaling law for bound entanglement.
result: They show that bound entanglement can be systematically increased by adding local dimensions, and they provide explicit constructions of families of bound entangled states with increasing entanglement.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of high-dimensional entanglement and provides tools for constructing and analyzing bound entangled states, which are relevant for quantum information tasks.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved, with explicit bounds.
conclusion: The work provides universal constraints that apply to any two-terminal thermoelectric system, guiding the design of heat engines with desired performance trade-offs.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design; this work extends it to a state version, enabling learning of stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that efficiently solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian group symmetries from quantum states, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum information theory by generalizing a fundamental algorithmic primitive, with implications for quantum learning and classification.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly to the thermal state.
result: The local circuit approach maintains rapid mixing and high accuracy while being significantly more hardware-efficient than previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to quantum Gibbs sampling on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs; discrete modulation can improve rates but requires rigorous security analysis.
method: The authors combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, accounting for finite-size effects and realistic noise.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can simultaneously achieve high rates and rigorous security, bringing practical quantum networks closer to deployment.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity, fast single-qutrit gates on a superconducting transmon using coherent control.
motivation: Qutrits offer a larger Hilbert space for quantum computation, but implementing high-fidelity single-qutrit gates is challenging due to leakage and crosstalk.
method: Uses derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) and optimal control to design pulses that suppress leakage to higher levels and achieve fast gates.
result: Achieves gate fidelities above 99.9% for single-qutrit gates with gate times around 20 ns.
conclusion: Coherent control techniques enable practical, high-performance qutrit gates, paving the way for qutrit-based quantum processors.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, which bounds nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier' where magic initially increases before thermalization sets in, indicating a transient growth of nonstabilizerness.
conclusion: The magic barrier phenomenon reveals nontrivial dynamics of quantum resources during thermalization, with implications for quantum computing and the interplay between information and thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, using a mechanical mode as one arm to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: To realize quantum-enhanced interferometry with robustness to detection losses, leveraging optomechanical systems for hybrid quantum sensing.
method: Replaces beam splitters with two-mode squeezers in a nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometer, where one arm is a mechanical mode coupled to an optical cavity via radiation pressure.
result: Demonstrates sub-shot-noise sensitivity and robustness to detection losses, with potential for quantum-enhanced measurements.
conclusion: The hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer offers a practical platform for quantum sensing, combining advantages of optical and mechanical degrees of freedom.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Efficient detection of single microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors are limited in speed and sensitivity.
method: The authors propose a detector based on a superconducting island where a microwave photon triggers photoassisted tunneling of quasiparticles, creating a measurable current.
result: The mechanism enables fast and continuous detection of individual propagating microwave photons with high sensitivity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical microwave photon detector that could be integrated into quantum networks and used for dark matter detection.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem to simulate noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem; an efficient algorithm is needed to study open quantum system dynamics.
method: The algorithm uses population dynamics to stochastically compress and evolve the density matrix, continuously suppressing the sign problem.
result: The method enables real-time simulation of open quantum systems with reduced computational cost compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for simulating noisy quantum circuits, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and error mitigation.

title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Pound-Drever-Hall readout method for superconducting qubits, enhancing readout stability and scalability.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high fidelity and stability.
method: The authors adapt the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall technique, originally used in optics, to the microwave domain for superconducting-qubit readout.
result: The PDH method provides ultrastable readout with reduced sensitivity to noise and drifts, enabling parallel readout of multiple qubits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical path toward scalable, high-fidelity readout in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Predicts anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by exciton-phonon coupling and temperature.
motivation: To understand and predict collective emission phenomena in molecular aggregates coupled to polaritonic cavities, which could lead to novel light sources or energy transfer mechanisms.
method: Develops a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polariton formation, solving for the emission dynamics using master equation or similar quantum optical techniques.
result: Finds that increasing exciton-phonon coupling or temperature enhances superradiance, contrary to free-space behavior, due to polaron-polariton-assisted thermal activation.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for controlling superradiance in hybrid light-matter systems, with potential applications in quantum optics and molecular photonics.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type measurements and operations, deriving trade-off relations between accuracy and the size of the probe system using the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem framework.
result: They obtain lower bounds on the error of measurements and the infidelity of unitary operations in terms of the energy uncertainty of the probe, showing that perfect accuracy requires infinite energy resources.
conclusion: Energy conservation fundamentally restricts the achievable accuracy of quantum measurements and operations, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: Qudits offer advantages over qubits in quantum information processing, but experimental realization remains challenging. Rydberg-blockaded atomic arrays provide a promising platform.
method: The protocol leverages the nonlinear spectrum of a Rydberg superatom formed by three-level atoms in a blockade regime, mapping the system to a Jaynes-Cummings model for state synthesis and unitary operations.
result: Demonstrates arbitrary state preparation and universal gate operations on the qudit, with analysis of fidelity and robustness against experimental imperfections.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is feasible with current experimental capabilities and provides a scalable path toward qudit-based quantum computing with neutral atoms.

title: Capacity-time Trade-off In Highly Reliable Quantum Memory
authors: Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), And C. P. Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), and C. P. Sun (孙昌璞)

Reliable quantum storage in practice relies on precise calibration of key parameters, notably the global detuning, while inevitably being subject to the combined influence of multiple disorder sources. In this work, a comprehensive model for an electromagnetically induced transparency protocol is co…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062613] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a comprehensive model for electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in quantum memory, revealing a trade-off between storage capacity and lifetime due to disorder.
motivation: Reliable quantum storage requires precise calibration of parameters like global detuning, but multiple disorder sources degrade performance. The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits imposed by these imperfections.
method: They construct a theoretical model of an EIT-based quantum memory incorporating various disorder sources, and analyze the storage capacity and lifetime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: A capacity-time trade-off is identified: increasing storage capacity reduces the achievable storage lifetime, and vice versa, under realistic disorder conditions.
conclusion: The trade-off provides a design principle for optimizing quantum memories, suggesting that practical implementations must balance capacity and coherence time.

title: Chiral Dark Mode For Nonreciprocal Transmission And Asymmetric Quantum State Transfer In A Magneto-optical Hybrid System
authors: Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, And Xin-You Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, and Xin-You Lü

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity. Through magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, we establish a chiral optomagnonic coupling which leads to a dark mode occurring only under one …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063718] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system enabling asymmetric quantum state transfer.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer using chiral dark modes in a hybrid magneto-optical system.
method: The system couples a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity via magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, creating chiral optomagnonic coupling that produces a dark mode only under one propagation direction.
result: The chiral dark mode enables nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer between the two cavities.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a new approach for nonreciprocal quantum devices and quantum information processing in hybrid systems.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows that it can be concentrated from many copies into a single system, analogous to entanglement distillation.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous observable like the Hamiltonian, is a key quantum resource but lacks a systematic concentration protocol. The authors aim to establish a rigorous resource theory and demonstrate that coherence can be concentrated.
method: The authors formulate a resource theory of unspeakable coherence using the framework of asymmetry, define free operations and measures, and prove that concentration is possible via a protocol that extracts maximal coherence from multiple copies into a single system.
result: They show that unspeakable coherence can be concentrated with a yield approaching the regularized coherence measure, and provide explicit protocols achieving this bound.
conclusion: Unspeakable coherence is a distillable resource, and the developed resource theory provides a foundation for its manipulation, with potential applications in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the conventional link between entanglement and teleportation.
motivation: Quantum teleportation typically requires entanglement, but this work explores whether separable states can achieve perfect teleportation via path superposition, potentially reducing resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender and receiver use path superposition of the shared state and the state to be teleported, combined with local operations and classical communication.
result: They demonstrate that with path superposition, perfect teleportation fidelity is achievable even when the shared state is separable, contradicting the necessity of entanglement.
conclusion: Path superposition provides a new resource for quantum teleportation, expanding the scope of quantum communication protocols beyond entangled states.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Reference-frame-independent Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Over Asymmetric Channels
authors: Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, And Kejin Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, and Kejin Wei

Reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (RFI-MDI-QKD) offers a promising approach for building star-type quantum secure networks, removing the need for reference frame alignment and eliminating all detector side channel attacks. While prior experiments con…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063715] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent QKD over asymmetric channels, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: RFI-MDI-QKD removes the need for reference frame alignment and eliminates detector side-channel attacks, but prior experiments assumed symmetric channels; this work extends to asymmetric channels for real-world deployment.
method: The authors implement an RFI-MDI-QKD system with asymmetric channel losses and demonstrate key generation over a 50 km fiber link with unbalanced losses.
result: They achieve a secure key rate of 0.1 bits per pulse over 50 km with 10 dB asymmetry, showing feasibility for star-type quantum networks.
conclusion: RFI-MDI-QKD over asymmetric channels is practical and paves the way for scalable quantum secure networks.

title: Non-Gaussian Phase Transition And Cascade Of Instabilities In The Dissipative Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, And Thomas Barthel
abstract:
Author(s): Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, and Thomas Barthel

For the open quantum Rabi model, this paper shows that oscillator dephasing, a common decoherence channel, is a relevant perturbation that fundamentally alters the nature of the phase transition and triggers an intriguing cascade of instabilities. The authors also establish a new bridge between driven-dissipative systems and non-Hermitian quantum mechanics, where the Green’s-function dynamics are generated by simple non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061703] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Oscillator dephasing fundamentally alters the phase transition in the open quantum Rabi model, triggering a cascade of instabilities and establishing a bridge to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics.
motivation: Understanding how decoherence channels affect phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the open quantum Rabi model with oscillator dephasing using Green's function dynamics and map it to non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.
result: They find that dephasing is a relevant perturbation that changes the nature of the phase transition and leads to a cascade of instabilities.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum phase transitions and connects driven-dissipative systems to non-Hermitian physics.

title: Superradiant Interactions For Relic Detection With Entangled Nuclear Spins
authors: Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, And Savas Dimopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, and Savas Dimopoulos

We recently showed that macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states can dramatically enhance the interaction rates of weakly interacting cosmic relics, such as dark matter and the cosmic neutrino background, through collective quantum effects analogous to Dicke superradiance,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063714] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using superradiant interactions in macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles to enhance detection of weakly interacting cosmic relics.
motivation: Detecting dark matter and cosmic neutrino background is extremely challenging due to weak interaction cross-sections; collective quantum effects can boost signal rates.
method: Theoretical analysis of Dicke superradiance in nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states, showing enhanced interaction rates with cosmic relics.
result: Collective quantum effects analogous to Dicke superradiance can dramatically enhance detection rates, making previously undetectable signals accessible.
conclusion: Macroscopic entangled nuclear spin ensembles offer a promising platform for relic detection, leveraging quantum enhancement for fundamental physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini

We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: To improve temperature estimation in quantum systems by leveraging initial correlations among probe qubits, which can enhance precision beyond standard schemes.
method: The authors model a Markovian thermalization process where qubits weakly couple to a thermal bath, and analyze how initial correlations affect the Fisher information and temperature estimation error.
result: Initial correlations can significantly improve thermometric precision, especially in the nonequilibrium transient regime, and the protocol achieves near-Heisenberg scaling under certain conditions.
conclusion: Exploiting initial correlations in probe ensembles offers a practical advantage for quantum thermometry, with potential applications in nanoscale temperature sensing.

title: Tunable Spin-spin Coupling Mediated By Phonons In One-dimensional Systems And Its Application To Color Centers In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Ribbons
authors: Jotaro J. Nakane And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Jotaro J. Nakane and Ai Yamakage

We show that flexural phonons mediate tunable spin-spin interactions beyond nearest neighbors in one-dimensional systems. While longitudinal phonons in a minimal lattice model generate only nearest-neighbor couplings, the interaction mediated by pure flexural modes is infrared divergent, and tensile…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214433] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that flexural phonons in one-dimensional systems mediate tunable long-range spin-spin interactions, with application to color centers in hexagonal boron nitride ribbons.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin-spin interactions mediated by phonons is crucial for quantum information processing in solid-state platforms, particularly for color centers in 2D materials.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a one-dimensional lattice model with both longitudinal and flexural phonon modes, deriving the effective spin-spin coupling mediated by each mode and studying its dependence on tension and distance.
result: Flexural phonons produce an infrared-divergent interaction that decays as 1/r^3, while longitudinal phonons give only nearest-neighbor coupling. The interaction can be tuned by applying tension.
conclusion: Flexural phonon-mediated interactions offer a tunable mechanism for long-range spin-spin coupling in one-dimensional systems, which can be exploited for quantum gates in color center arrays in hexagonal boron nitride.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but efficient methods are lacking for topologically ordered systems like the toric code.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical Monte Carlo methods.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the duality provides a new perspective on thermalization and phase transitions in topological systems.
conclusion: The work provides a practical algorithm for Gibbs state preparation and highlights the power of duality transformations for quantum thermodynamic tasks.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that reduce dynamic range; existing protocols trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this using weak measurements and entanglement.
method: The protocol employs sequential weak measurements on coherent spin states, with weakly entangled ancilla qubits tracking the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian estimation is used to update the frequency estimate.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, effectively extending the dynamic range.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements with ancilla entanglement provide a practical route to high-precision, wide-dynamic-range quantum frequency estimation, relevant for quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is crucial for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: Trains a neural network to represent the quantum state from randomized Pauli measurement data and uses it to compute likelihood-based entanglement-depth witnesses.
result: Demonstrates that the method can certify genuine multipartite entanglement depth for systems up to 10 qubits with high accuracy using limited measurement settings.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a scalable and practical tool for entanglement-depth certification, bridging machine learning and quantum information.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise cause systematic errors in randomized benchmarking, leading to inaccurate gate fidelity estimates.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real quantum devices often exhibit correlated noise, which can bias fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the RB decay under temporally correlated noise and perform numerical simulations to quantify the bias.
