result: They show that temporal correlations can lead to significant over- or under-estimation of average gate fidelity, and propose a modified protocol to mitigate these errors.
conclusion: Temporal correlations are a blind spot for standard RB, and accounting for them is crucial for reliable characterization of quantum gates.

title: Distributing Entanglement At The Quantum Speed Limit In Rydberg Chains
authors: Kent Ueno And Alexandre Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Kent Ueno and Alexandre Cooper

We numerically study the transport of Rydberg excitations in chains of neutral atoms. We realize an effective flip-flop interaction using off-resonant driving fields. By tuning the relative distances between atoms and applying atom-selective detuning fields, we fulfill the perfect transport conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023260] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of entanglement transport in Rydberg atom chains achieving near quantum speed limit via off-resonant driving and atom-selective detuning.
motivation: To understand and optimize the distribution of entanglement in neutral atom chains, which is crucial for quantum networking and quantum information processing.
method: Numerical simulation of Rydberg excitation transport using an effective flip-flop interaction realized by off-resonant driving fields, with tunable interatomic distances and detuning to satisfy perfect transport conditions.
result: The protocol achieves entanglement transport at the quantum speed limit, with high fidelity and minimal decoherence.
conclusion: Rydberg atom chains can serve as efficient quantum channels for distributing entanglement, with performance approaching fundamental speed limits.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding how to minimize work in active systems is important for designing efficient nanoscale machines and for fundamental thermodynamics of active matter.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework based on a Langevin equation for an odd tracer with active fluctuations, and apply optimal control theory to find the protocol that minimizes the mean work for a given displacement.
result: They derive analytical expressions for the optimal trap translation protocol and the corresponding minimal work, showing that odd mobility and viscoelasticity significantly affect the optimal strategy and work cost.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermodynamic control of active systems, with potential applications in active matter and biophysics.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong magnon-photon coupling in magnetic insulator thin films using a modular loop-gap resonator design.
motivation: To achieve strong coupling between magnons and photons in thin-film magnetic insulators, which is important for hybrid quantum systems and cavity magnonics.
method: Designs and fabricates a loop-gap resonator optimized for thin films, and measures the coupling strength via microwave spectroscopy.
result: Achieves strong magnon-photon coupling with cooperativity >1 in thin-film yttrium iron garnet (YIG) samples.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators are effective for realizing strong coupling in thin-film geometries, enabling compact hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; a robust approach is needed for practical scalability.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are naturally insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being immune to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging the noise-rejection properties of Lieb-Mattis states.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of motion are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a combination of laser pulses and motional state engineering to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical nature.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex motional states, with applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms via coupling to an auxiliary Rydberg atom array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical readout and manipulation.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control of circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing; radiation-induced errors are a known but poorly characterized source.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using a combination of qubit readout and noise spectroscopy.
result: They observe correlated phase error bursts that occur simultaneously across multiple qubits, with rates that persist despite state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase errors from ionizing radiation pose a fundamental challenge to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum computing and thermodynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in many-body chaotic systems.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the absence of a true Trotterization transition in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate due to many degrees of freedom; a reduced model that preserves only observable dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively discarding fast degrees of freedom that are not resolved by measurements.
result: The technique yields accurate reduced models for several examples, demonstrating that observable dynamics can be captured with significantly fewer degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a promising tool for simulating open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. This work aims to overcome these limitations.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading with minimal atom loss, enabling continuous operation of the atom array.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques provide a practical route to scalable, high-performance neutral-atom quantum computing platforms.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded superradiance and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded ferromagnetic phases and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg arrays provides a platform for realizing kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generation (QRNG) provides provably secure randomness without trusting the devices, but previous implementations were bulky. This work aims to miniaturize such systems onto a photonic chip for practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing QRNG protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control logic, using standard CMOS-compatible processes.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with a certified min-entropy, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion in a compact, scalable platform.
conclusion: This work shows that self-testing QRNG can be realized on an integrated photonic chip, paving the way for production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action formalism combined with computer algebra to systematically optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols.
result: The new method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in benchmark systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems typically scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to classical additive codes, enabling the construction of k-local sequences that cancel spatially correlated noise up to order k.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, and can be tailored to specific noise models using code properties.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation in optomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, which combines deterministic and randomized product formulas to reduce the simulation error and thus the required circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized product formulas offer a practical and efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, possibly including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking and highlights the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems, relevant for quantum simulators.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol for multilevel quantum systems (qudits) that improves nondemolition measurement fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Standard quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the ability to perform repeated or sequential measurements. This work aims to enhance the nondemolition nature of measurements in qudit systems, which is crucial for quantum error correction and quantum information processing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, thereby minimizing back-action and improving readout fidelity.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% for a qudit system, significantly outperforming non-adaptive methods, and reduces measurement-induced errors and overall measurement time.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for improving quantum measurements in multilevel systems, with potential applications across various qubit platforms, including silicon quantum dots and superconducting qubits.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations improves simulation accuracy by sevenfold.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors and use it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when simulating variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and analyze its projected ensemble to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and relate it to out-of-time-ordered correlators and other chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: The approach provides a unified framework for probing chaos in open quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum thermalization and information scrambling.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including stabilizer formalism and resource theory of magic, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required for random unitary ensembles.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales extensively with the number of qubits, implying that shallow circuits cannot generate high-quality pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental resource-theoretic limitation on generating pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast and noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems to resolve key processes and parity dynamics.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry to probe a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to infer the state of the system.
result: The technique resolves key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a promising readout method for Majorana-based qubits, enabling fast and noninvasive measurements.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
method: The paper surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental implementations (CV-QKD, entanglement distribution, quantum networks).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with demonstrated field trials and high-rate QKD systems.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for scalable quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in long-distance distribution and integration with repeaters.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking to known equilibrium universality classes and new nonequilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive classification that guides future theoretical and experimental work on driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting coherence times is crucial for developing solid-state spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of long-coherence spin qubits.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as current theories lack experimental verification; information-theoretic methods provide a novel way to constrain possible theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement, nonlocality) to design tabletop experiments that probe the quantum nature of gravity.
result: It analyzes proposed gravitationally induced entanglement experiments, showing they can test whether gravity is a quantum mediator, and discusses their feasibility and implications.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a promising path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with several tabletop experiments potentially realizable in the near future.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication in exotic spacetime scenarios, such as those involving closed timelike curves, provides insights into the interplay between quantum information and general relativity.
method: The authors model the noisy postselected closed timelike curve as a quantum channel and derive its retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic techniques.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity, showing it is given by a formula involving the channel's entanglement-assisted capacity.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous framework for retrocausal communication and highlights the role of entanglement in such settings.

title: Adaptable Route To Fast Coherent State Transport Via Bang-Bang-Bang Protocols
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, and H. H. Jen

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an adaptable bang-bang-bang protocol for fast coherent state transport of atomic qubits, achieving high fidelity in reduced time.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow and limits quantum operations; faster transport is needed for efficient quantum computation.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence with optimized pulse durations to steer the atomic state along a desired path, minimizing leakage and phase errors.
result: Demonstrates near-unit fidelity transport in times significantly shorter than adiabatic limits, with robustness to parameter variations.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, fast, and high-fidelity method for coherent state transport, applicable to atomic qubit platforms.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the imaginarity of measurements affects entanglement concentration, showing that using complex-valued measurements can increase the yield of maximally entangled states from partially entangled ones.
motivation: Understanding the role of complex numbers in quantum theory as a resource, and exploring whether imaginarity can enhance entanglement manipulation tasks.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for imaginarity in measurements and apply it to the entanglement concentration protocol, analyzing the trade-off between measurement imaginarity and the yield of Bell states.
result: They find that measurements with higher imaginarity can achieve higher entanglement concentration yields, and they derive bounds relating the imaginarity of measurements to the achievable entanglement fidelity.
conclusion: Imaginarity in measurements is a useful resource for entanglement concentration, and the results highlight the operational significance of complex numbers in quantum information processing.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To realize and characterize a higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect, which extends the conventional spin Hall effect to high-spin systems and may enable new forms of spin current generation.
method: A single trapped ion is used to simulate the spin-orbit coupling and measure the spin tensor Hall conductivity via state-dependent fluorescence and coherent manipulation.
result: The observed spin tensor Hall conductivity matches theoretical predictions and exhibits universality robust to parameter variations.
conclusion: The trapped ion platform successfully demonstrates a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect, validating theoretical predictions and opening avenues for studying higher-rank spin transport.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics scheme for generating n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundles via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are useful for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses a cavity magnomechanics system with resonant driving to induce super Rabi oscillations via the Barnett effect, then relies on dissipative dynamics to generate the bundles.
result: Demonstrates that n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be realized with tunable parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new way to generate nonclassical states in hybrid magnomechanical systems, relevant for quantum networking and transduction.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Separable Squeezed States In Finite-memory Structured Reservoir
authors: Austen Couvertier And Ting Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Austen Couvertier and Ting Yu

Entanglement in continuous-variable Gaussian systems is a key resource, and common reservoirs can both suppress and generate correlations. Existing work focused on preentangled states or Markovian baths, leaving open whether separable squeezed inputs entangle in structured environments or under modu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063724] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement generation from separable squeezed states in a finite-memory structured reservoir, extending beyond Markovian and preentangled assumptions.
motivation: Understanding how structured environments can generate entanglement from initially separable states is important for continuous-variable quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of two squeezed states coupled to a common non-Markovian reservoir with finite memory, using exact master equations and solving for the covariance matrix.
result: They find that entanglement can be generated from separable squeezed inputs under certain conditions, and the reservoir memory and squeezing parameters significantly affect the entanglement dynamics.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs can serve as a resource for entanglement generation in continuous-variable systems, with potential applications in quantum communication and information processing.

title: Beyond Qubits: Multilevel Quantum Sensing For Dark Matter
authors: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, And Ernst David Herbschleb
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, and Ernst David Herbschleb

Quantum sensing with qubits has advanced fundamental physics searches, but higher dimensional systems offer largely unexplored potential. We show that in ultralight dark matter searches spin-1 NV-center qutrits exploiting common mode noise suppression achieve an order of magnitude improvement in axi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060802] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Using spin-1 NV-center qutrits for ultralight dark matter sensing achieves an order of magnitude improvement in sensitivity via common mode noise suppression.
motivation: Quantum sensing with qubits has advanced fundamental physics searches, but higher-dimensional systems like qutrits offer unexplored potential for improved sensitivity.
method: The authors propose using spin-1 NV centers as qutrits, exploiting common mode noise suppression techniques to enhance detection of ultralight dark matter.
result: An order of magnitude improvement in sensitivity for axion-like dark matter detection is demonstrated compared to qubit-based approaches.
conclusion: Multilevel quantum sensors, specifically NV-center qutrits, provide a promising platform for dark matter searches, leveraging noise suppression to outperform qubit sensors.

title: Nonadiabatic Self-healing Of Trotter Errors In Digitized Counterdiabatic Dynamics
authors: Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, And Koushik Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, and Koushik Paul

Trotter errors in digitized quantum dynamics arise from approximating time-ordered evolution under noncommuting Hamiltonian terms with a product formula. In the adiabatic regime, such errors are known to exhibit long-time self-healing [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that Trotter errors in digitized counterdiabatic dynamics can self-heal nonadiabatically, improving the fidelity of quantum simulations.
motivation: Trotter errors limit the accuracy of digital quantum simulation; understanding and mitigating these errors is crucial for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze digitized counterdiabatic dynamics using a product formula and derive conditions under which Trotter errors self-heal even outside the adiabatic regime.
result: They show that nonadiabatic self-healing occurs, leading to reduced error accumulation and higher fidelity for certain driving protocols.
conclusion: Nonadiabatic self-healing of Trotter errors can be exploited to design more efficient quantum simulations without requiring full adiabaticity.

title: Oh Molecule As A Quantum Probe To Jointly Estimate Electric And Magnetic Fields
authors: Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, And Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, and Matteo G. A. Paris

The hydroxyl radical (the OH molecule) carries both electric and magnetic dipole moments and, as a diatomic molecule, admits a comparatively simple and accurate model. This makes it a natural quantum probe for the joint estimation of electric and magnetic fields. Here we study simultaneous estimatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062612] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The OH molecule is proposed as a quantum probe for simultaneous estimation of electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: To exploit the OH molecule's dual dipole moments for joint field sensing, leveraging its simple model.
method: Theoretical analysis of simultaneous estimation using quantum parameter estimation theory.
result: The OH molecule enables efficient joint estimation with performance close to the quantum limit.
conclusion: The OH molecule is a promising platform for multi-parameter quantum sensing.

title: Non-Markovianity-based Ultrasensitive Parameter Estimation
authors: Olli Siltanen
abstract:
Author(s): Olli Siltanen

Accurate parameter estimation is a central task in quantum metrology and sensing, where quantum resources can provide precision beyond classical limits. In realistic settings, however, system-environment interactions lead to decoherence, reducing these strategies to their classical counterparts. Noi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062427] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovianity can enhance parameter estimation precision beyond the standard quantum limit, even in the presence of noise.
motivation: Quantum metrology suffers from decoherence due to system-environment interactions, which typically degrades precision. Non-Markovian memory effects might be exploited to counteract this.
method: The authors analyze a qubit probe coupled to a structured environment, using a non-Markovian master equation and calculating the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation.
result: They find that non-Markovianity can lead to a scaling of precision that surpasses the standard quantum limit, and that the enhancement is linked to the revival of quantum coherence.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity is a resource for ultrasensitive parameter estimation, offering a new avenue for quantum metrology in realistic noisy environments.

title: Two-dimensional Quon Language: Unifying Framework For Cliffords, Matchgates, And Beyond
authors: Byungmin Kang, Chen Zhao, Zhengwei Liu, Xun Gao, And Soonwon Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Byungmin Kang, Chen Zhao, Zhengwei Liu, Xun Gao, and Soonwon Choi

Simulating generic quantum states and dynamics is practically intractable using classical computers. However, certain special classes—namely, Clifford and matchgate circuits—permit efficient computation. They provide invaluable tools for studying many-body physics, quantum chemistry, and quantum com…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unified framework for Clifford and matchgate circuits using quon language, enabling efficient classical simulation of a broader class of quantum circuits.
motivation: Clifford and matchgate circuits are important for quantum computation but have limited scope; a unified framework could extend efficient simulability to new circuit families.
method: The authors develop a two-dimensional quon language based on anyon-like fusion rules and braiding, which captures both Clifford and matchgate operations as special cases.
result: They show that the quon language encompasses a larger class of circuits that remain classically simulable, and provide explicit algorithms for simulation.
conclusion: This work provides a unifying perspective on efficiently simulable quantum circuits and may lead to new insights in quantum computation and many-body physics.

title: Direct Observation Of Dynamical Quasicondensation And Generalized Thermalization On Different Quantum Computing Platforms
authors: Philipp Frey And Stephan Rachel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Frey and Stephan Rachel

Hard-core bosons (HCBs) in one dimension display striking nonequilibrium phenomena, including the dynamical formation of quasicondensates at finite momentum and generalized thermalization to a generalized Gibbs ensemble (GGE). These effects, rooted in the integrability of the HCB model, have been ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224306] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization of hard-core bosons on quantum computing platforms, demonstrating non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To experimentally verify theoretical predictions of dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization in integrable systems using quantum computers.
method: Simulations of hard-core bosons on IBM and Quantinuum quantum processors, using trotterized time evolution and measuring momentum distributions and correlation functions.
result: Clear signatures of dynamical quasicondensation and relaxation to a generalized Gibbs ensemble were observed, matching theoretical expectations.
conclusion: Quantum computers can serve as reliable platforms for studying non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics and thermalization.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains essential physics while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the master equation to be solved more efficiently, and demonstrate the approach on example systems.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for non-Markovian systems with significantly reduced computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This technique makes non-Markovian master equations more accessible for practical simulations, enabling broader study of open quantum systems.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical behavior in the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models, protected by self-duality.
motivation: To understand dynamical phase transitions and multicriticality in stochastic systems, which are relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of kinetically constrained models using large deviation theory and identify lines of self-duality that protect multicritical points.
result: They demonstrate the existence of dynamical phases separated by self-dual lines and uncover multicritical points where these lines meet.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic dynamics, offering a new perspective on dynamical phase transitions.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple molecular systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: Understanding how primitive life could harvest energy without complex enzymatic machinery is a fundamental question in origins-of-life research.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a molecular system that extracts work from cyclic changes in environmental conditions (e.g., pH, temperature) via a ratchet-like mechanism.
result: They show that such cyclic environments can drive the synthesis of high-energy molecules (e.g., ATP analogs) and maintain non-equilibrium steady states, providing a robust energy harvesting pathway.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental fluctuations can serve as a simple, generic energy source for prebiotic chemical systems, offering a plausible route to the emergence of metabolism.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems by combining real-time quantum dynamics with classical Lanczos post-processing.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is computationally hard for classical methods, especially at low temperatures; quantum computers may offer a speedup.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses a quantum computer to generate a Krylov subspace via real-time evolution, then classically diagonalizes the Hamiltonian in that subspace to compute thermal observables.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems and shows accurate results for thermal expectation values, with potential advantages in scaling compared to classical methods.
conclusion: QFTLM provides a hybrid quantum-classical approach to finite-temperature simulations, leveraging near-term quantum devices for a classically challenging problem.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a metabolic quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography by combining the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural currents.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on the information that can be extracted from brain activity via MEG, given the metabolic constraints of neural tissue.
method: The authors combine the quantum energy resolution limit for magnetic field sensing with the metabolic power budget of neural currents to derive an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: They find that the information capacity is fundamentally limited by the metabolic power available, leading to a quantum-metabolic bound that is orders of magnitude below the classical Shannon limit.
conclusion: The metabolic quantum limit imposes a fundamental constraint on MEG's ability to resolve neural activity, suggesting that further improvements in sensor sensitivity may not translate into increased information without considering metabolic costs.

title: Identifying Nonequilibrium Degrees Of Freedom In High-dimensional Stochastic Systems
authors: Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, And Gautam Reddy
abstract:
Author(s): Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, and Gautam Reddy

Any coarse-grained description of a nonequilibrium system should faithfully represent its latent irreversible degrees of freedom. However, standard dimensionality reduction methods typically prioritize accurate reconstruction over physical relevance. Here, we introduce a model-free approach to ident…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023264] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method to identify latent irreversible degrees of freedom in high-dimensional stochastic systems.
motivation: Standard dimensionality reduction methods prioritize reconstruction over physical relevance, missing nonequilibrium degrees of freedom.
method: Introduces a data-driven approach based on the asymmetry of the covariance matrix of time-lagged increments to detect irreversible components.
result: Successfully identifies nonequilibrium degrees of freedom in synthetic and real-world high-dimensional stochastic systems.
conclusion: The method provides a physically meaningful coarse-graining for nonequilibrium systems, aiding in understanding their thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which is relevant for understanding fluctuations and thermodynamics in non-equilibrium systems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and showing convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that bridges jump and diffusion processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across different scales.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics, with potential applications in information thermodynamics and small-scale systems.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates, through phase transitions, can process high-dimensional environmental information, linking phase separation to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, thermodynamic mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework and review evidence that biomolecular condensation can implement computations like sensing, classification, and response, drawing analogies to physical systems.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform high-dimensional information processing efficiently, with examples from biology and potential design principles.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation represents a powerful, underappreciated paradigm for cellular computation, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated on neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method uses single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from single-shot measurements, demonstrating its effectiveness on a qubit platform.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, which can aid in understanding and mitigating decoherence.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated, enabling megaquop-scale computations with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum simulators more practical for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation, advancing the feasibility of quantum advantage in this platform.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
