motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra. They use tools from random matrix theory and representation theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to a non-vanishing variance of the loss function, thus mitigating barren plateaus. The concentration is linked to the noise rate and circuit depth.
conclusion: Noise, often detrimental, can be beneficial for trainability in variational quantum algorithms by reducing expressivity. This provides a principled way to design noise-resilient circuits and optimize training.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Implements a trapped-ion quantum processor with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies.
result: Achieves a molecular energy computation with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry on current hardware.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis will help researchers navigate the landscape of non-Markovian simulation methods and advance the field.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and circuit depth.
motivation: Qudits can reduce the complexity of quantum circuits by replacing multiple qubits with a single qudit, potentially simplifying hardware requirements and improving error rates.
method: The paper surveys theoretical embeddings of qubits into qudits, decomposition techniques for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Key examples show that a single qutrit can implement a Toffoli gate with fewer operations than the standard qubit decomposition, and qudit-based algorithms can reduce circuit depth.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising alternative for quantum computing, especially in near-term devices, but challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, proposing a framework to quantify and characterize their distinguishability.
motivation: Quantum state distinguishability is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing, but non-Gaussian states are less understood than Gaussian ones.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination and information-theoretic measures to analyze non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states are distinguishable and quantify the advantage over Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for using non-Gaussian states in quantum information tasks, though the results are primarily theoretical and not directly tied to core quantum information topics like entanglement or cryptography.

title: Universal Composite Phase Gates With Tunable Target Phase
authors: Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, And Andon A. Rangelov
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, and Andon A. Rangelov

We present a systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with a continuously tunable target phase. Using a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of the single-pulse propagator, we design gates from an even number of nominal [MATH] pulses and derive analytic phase families by cance…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with continuously tunable target phase using Cayley-Klein parametrization.
motivation: Composite pulses are essential for robust quantum control, but existing methods often fix the target phase; this work aims to provide tunability for greater flexibility in quantum gates.
method: The authors use a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of single-pulse propagators and design gates from an even number of nominal π pulses, deriving analytic phase families by canceling error terms.
result: They demonstrate universal composite phase gates that can achieve any target phase while maintaining robustness against pulse area errors.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a versatile tool for quantum control, enabling precise phase manipulation in quantum information processing.

title: Error Convergence Of Quantum Linear System Solvers
authors: Matias Ginzburg And Ugo Marzolino
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Ginzburg and Ugo Marzolino

The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm remains a paradigmatic quantum routine for solving linear systems and a widely used benchmark in theoretical and experimental studies. Several circuit-level variants have been proposed to simplify its implementation, including constructions in which the cloc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062436] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the error convergence of quantum linear system solvers, focusing on the HHL algorithm and its variants.
motivation: Understanding the error behavior of quantum linear system solvers is crucial for practical implementation and benchmarking.
method: The authors study the convergence of errors in HHL-type algorithms, considering different clock constructions and noise models.
result: They derive bounds on the error as a function of the number of qubits and circuit depth, showing trade-offs between accuracy and resource requirements.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the practical limitations of quantum linear system solvers, but does not introduce new information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.

title: Hardware-efficient Quantum Annealing With Error Mitigation Via Classical Shadow
authors: Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Yuichiro Matsuzaki
abstract:
Author(s): Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Yuichiro Matsuzaki

Quantum annealing (QA) is an efficient method for finding the ground-state energy of the problem Hamiltonian. However, in practical implementation, the system suffers from decoherence. Recently, “localized virtual purification” (LVP) was proposed to suppress decoherence in the context of noisy inter…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062430] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient quantum annealing protocol with error mitigation using classical shadow techniques.
motivation: Quantum annealing suffers from decoherence; existing error mitigation methods like LVP are resource-intensive. The authors aim to reduce measurement overhead.
method: Combines quantum annealing with classical shadow tomography to estimate observables and mitigate errors with fewer measurements.
result: Demonstrates improved ground-state energy estimation accuracy with reduced measurement cost compared to standard LVP.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum annealers.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
authors: Liang He And Su Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions, breaking fundamental additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties, particularly in the Mott-insulator phase.
method: Theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization for small systems, focusing on the Mott-insulator limit.
result: The system shows non-additive thermodynamics, with anomalous scaling of entropy and specific heat, and violation of standard thermodynamic relations.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions lead to qualitatively new thermodynamic behavior that cannot be captured by standard statistical mechanics.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies and comparing their power to global operations.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of local operations in distinguishing quantum unitaries is fundamental for quantum information processing and communication.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies for unitary discrimination and analyze the optimal success probability using different probing states and measurements.
result: They provide a classification of LOCC strategies and show that global operations can outperform LOCC in certain cases, with explicit examples.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum channel discrimination under locality constraints, highlighting the gap between local and global distinguishability.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents optimizations for fault-tolerant cat state preparation, focusing on reducing resource overhead for large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them at large fault distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale well.
method: The authors propose a method to optimize the preparation of cat states by reducing the number of required qubits and gates, using a combination of stabilizer formalism and circuit synthesis techniques.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in qubit count and gate depth for cat states at various fault distances, enabling more efficient fault-tolerant protocols.
conclusion: The optimized cat state preparation reduces resource overhead, making fault-tolerant quantum computing more practical, though the work is primarily a circuit optimization rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Subsystem Gauge Symmetry Restoration
authors: Hao-Yue Qi And Wei Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Yue Qi and Wei Zheng

Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge. Recently, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon—has attracted considerable attention and has been extensively studied in systems with global symmetries. Here, we study the Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214311] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in the context of subsystem gauge symmetry restoration in a many-body system.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems is a central challenge, and the quantum Mpemba effect offers a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon that may reveal fundamental insights.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of subsystem gauge symmetry restoration using numerical simulations and analytical arguments, likely focusing on a specific lattice model.
result: They observe a quantum Mpemba effect where the subsystem gauge symmetry restores faster from a less symmetric initial state than from a more symmetric one.
conclusion: The work extends the study of the quantum Mpemba effect to gauge theories, providing new insights into relaxation dynamics in constrained systems.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
authors: Noa Feldman And Moshe Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor networks, showing that lattice discretization naturally reproduces universal corner terms.
motivation: Understanding universal features of entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, particularly corner contributions, is important for characterizing quantum phases.
method: The authors use tensor network methods (likely matrix product states or projected entangled pair states) to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with sharp corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution to entanglement entropy emerges naturally from lattice discretization and matches field theory predictions.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a viable approach to study universal entanglement properties in lattice models, bridging field theory and numerical simulations.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic theory is applied to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, which are anomalous.
conclusion: The work provides a hydrodynamic description of charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata, contributing to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improving VQE ansatz design for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.
method: Starts from an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information measures to construct an efficient ansatz.
result: Demonstrates efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems.
conclusion: The ansatz is efficient and accurate for atomic systems, showing promise for quantum chemistry.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Q-FLIP, an iterative method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced circuit depth and number of qubits.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML are resource-intensive, so reducing overhead is crucial.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns feature map parameters by alternating between classical optimization and quantum evaluation.
result: Demonstrates that Q-FLIP achieves comparable classification accuracy to standard methods while using significantly fewer gates and qubits.
conclusion: The method offers a practical way to implement quantum feature maps on near-term devices with limited resources.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize optical quantum state generation, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum computing and metrology, but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to improve success rates through better control.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond the stellar rank and develop a systematic optimization framework for optical non-Gaussian state generation.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating key non-Gaussian quantum states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for scalable generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of high-rate quantum LDPC codes, and a protocol for generating CCZ magic states in constant depth.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes enable magic state generation with high noise resilience and improved overhead compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points, reducing the need for quantum evaluations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to accelerate variational quantum algorithms by combining quantum and classical resources.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and Fisher information near critical points.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of how criticality can be exploited for precision metrology.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach but remains largely theoretical; experimental challenges persist.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a moment-matching technique to construct a unitary dilation on a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling efficient simulation of linear differential equations.
result: The proposed framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in open quantum systems and differential equations.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Simulating periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; a data-driven approach using neural operators can accelerate predictions.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, capturing temporal correlations.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond training data and learns effective Floquet Hamiltonians, demonstrating generalization.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for modeling time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The authors develop a technique to propagate errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: They demonstrate that their method scales efficiently for a large class of protocols, enabling classical simulation of previously intractable cases.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes by carefully designing the measurement sequence and leveraging the code structure.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining the code's distance and other properties, and is demonstrated on several families of LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for parallel logical measurements, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing with LDPC codes.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to fermionic systems, specifically Majorana-based qubits, and constructs high-rate codes and fault-tolerant operations.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana-based qubits requires tailored error correction protocols that respect fermionic parity constraints.
method: The authors generalize qubit-based fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic systems, designing gates, measurements, and codes that are compatible with Majorana modes.
result: They present high-rate quantum codes and explicit fault-tolerant operations for Majorana-based quantum computing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computation using Majorana qubits, but the contribution is primarily in quantum error correction rather than the researcher's core interests.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations for impulsive force measurements, with potential applications in dark matter searches.
motivation: To detect weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by surpassing the standard quantum limit of a mechanical oscillator.
method: The authors use a levitated nanoparticle in an optical trap and employ a pulsed measurement scheme to resolve forces below the zero-point motion.
result: They demonstrate force sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations, enabling detection of impulses as small as a few attonewton-seconds.
conclusion: This technique opens new possibilities for sensing tiny forces, including searches for dark matter and tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how environment-induced interactions affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms near a reflecting boundary.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the focus here is on a specific physical scenario rather than general information-theoretic results.
method: The authors use an open quantum systems framework, incorporating environment-induced energy shifts (atom-boundary and interatomic) to analyze entanglement dynamics.
result: They find that environment-induced interactions can either enhance or suppress entanglement depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement control in structured environments, but is more about a specific physical effect than advancing quantum information theory.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Spin-boson Model With A Continuous Bosonic Spectrum: Exceptional Points And Dynamics
authors: Yong-Xin Zhang And Qing-Hu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Xin Zhang and Qing-Hu Chen

This work studies a [MATH]-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model consisting of a non-Hermitian two-level system coupled to a continuous bosonic bath. The static properties of the system are analyzed through a projection method derived from the displacement operator. We find that only a si…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063723] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model with a continuous bosonic bath, focusing on exceptional points and dynamics.
motivation: To understand the static and dynamic properties of non-Hermitian quantum systems coupled to a bath, which may have implications for open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
method: A projection method derived from the displacement operator is used to analyze the static properties, and the dynamics are studied via the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
result: Only a single exceptional point is found, and the dynamics exhibit PT-symmetry breaking and revival phenomena.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric spin-boson model shows rich behavior but is not directly applicable to the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, exceeding the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to overcome this limitation using memory effects.
method: They analyze a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian derived from a non-Markovian master equation and study the coalescence of eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
result: Non-Markovianity allows multiple eigenvalues to become equal simultaneously, creating higher-order exceptional points beyond the conventional bound.
conclusion: Non-Markovian dynamics provide a mechanism to realize high-order exceptional points, which could be useful for sensing and control.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
authors: Jaromír Fiurášek
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are important for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; optimizing success probability is crucial.
method: The author uses a theoretical framework based on Gaussian states and photon-counting measurements, deriving upper bounds on heralding probabilities using semidefinite programming and analytical techniques.
result: Maximum heralding probabilities are obtained for various target states, showing trade-offs between state quality and success probability.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits and practical guidance for experimental generation of nonclassical states via heralding.

title: Feedback Cooling And Thermometry Of A Single Trapped Ion Using A Knife Edge
authors: Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, and Gerd Leuchs

We report on a simple and easy to implement method of feedback cooling trapped ions to temperatures below those achievable using only Doppler cooling. Additionally, the feedback cooling results in significantly shorter cooling times. For selected parameters, we demonstrate cooling to temperatures be…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063717] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates feedback cooling of a single trapped ion using a knife edge, achieving sub-Doppler temperatures and faster cooling.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but cooling to the motional ground state is essential for high-fidelity operations. Existing methods like Doppler cooling are limited, and more complex techniques (e.g., sideband cooling) require additional lasers.
method: A knife edge is placed near the ion to create a position-dependent fluorescence signal, which is used in a feedback loop to apply a damping force via an electric field, cooling the ion's motion.
result: The feedback cooling achieves temperatures below the Doppler limit and reduces cooling time significantly compared to Doppler cooling alone.
conclusion: This simple feedback method offers an alternative for cooling trapped ions without the need for resolved sideband cooling, potentially simplifying experimental setups.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for minimum uncertainty and squeezed states using a stronger sum uncertainty relation, which may offer new insights into quantum correlations.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation proposed by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and apply them to single-mode and two-mode systems, identifying squeezed states.
result: They show that the sum uncertainty relation yields a broader class of minimum uncertainty states, including squeezed states, and provides a tighter bound than the product relation.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation is a useful tool for characterizing non-classical states, but the results are primarily mathematical and do not directly advance core topics in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Complexity And Localization In Random And Time-periodic Unitary Circuits
authors: Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, And Pingal Pratyush Nath
abstract:
Author(s): Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, and Pingal Pratyush Nath

We study the growth and saturation of complexity in Krylov basis in random quantum circuits. In Haar-random unitary evolution, we show that, for large system sizes, this notion of complexity grows linearly before saturating at a late-time value of [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hilbert space dimension, at …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214312] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Studies Krylov complexity growth and saturation in random and time-periodic unitary circuits.
motivation: To understand quantum complexity in many-body systems and its relation to localization phenomena.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Krylov basis complexity in Haar-random and Floquet unitary circuits.
result: Complexity grows linearly and saturates at a value proportional to Hilbert space dimension; localization suppresses growth.
conclusion: Krylov complexity provides a useful probe of quantum dynamics and localization in random circuits.

title: Lieb-Robinson Causality And non-Fermi Liquids
authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, And Sean A. Hartnoll
abstract:
Author(s): Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, and Sean A. Hartnoll

Here, the authors show that the Lieb-Robinson causality bound, a fundamental result in quantum lattice physics, implies a first-principles and model-independent bound on certain non-Fermi liquid coupling constants. The work demonstrates that methods from the modern S-matrix bootstrap in high-energy physics — in particular, analyticity constraints in both the complex energy and momentum planes — can be adapted to condensed matter lattice models.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245125] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a bound on non-Fermi liquid coupling constants using Lieb-Robinson causality and S-matrix bootstrap methods.
motivation: To obtain first-principles, model-independent bounds on coupling constants in non-Fermi liquids, which are poorly understood strongly correlated systems.
method: Adapts analyticity constraints from the S-matrix bootstrap in high-energy physics to condensed matter lattice models, combined with the Lieb-Robinson bound.
result: Establishes a causality-based bound on certain non-Fermi liquid coupling constants.
conclusion: Lieb-Robinson causality can be used to constrain non-Fermi liquid parameters, demonstrating cross-fertilization between high-energy and condensed matter physics.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the temporal evolution of a demagnetized ferromagnetic state toward equilibrium using Baryakhtar's spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal spin relaxation.
motivation: Understanding how spin systems relax to equilibrium is fundamental to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but the paper focuses on a specific ferromagnetic system without clear connections to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.
method: The authors apply Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both relativistic (local) and exchange (nonlocal) spin relaxation mechanisms, to analyze the evolution of a nearly homogeneous demagnetized state.
result: They demonstrate that strong nonlocal relaxation can significantly alter the relaxation dynamics compared to purely local relaxation, leading to different temporal behaviors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spin relaxation in ferromagnets but does not address information-theoretic or thermodynamic constraints relevant to the user's core interests.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws and memory effects.
motivation: Understanding correlated motion in single-particle tracking is important for characterizing transport in complex environments, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function that depend on the memory kernel and noise properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing correlated displacements in classical stochastic dynamics, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: Resetting processes are a simple way to generate non-equilibrium steady states, and understanding underdamped dynamics is important for realistic physical systems where inertia matters.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for underdamped Brownian motion with Poissonian resetting, considering two resetting procedures: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while randomizing velocity according to a Maxwell distribution.
result: They derive exact expressions for the stationary probability distributions in position and velocity, and compute quantities like mean squared displacement and correlation functions.
conclusion: The two resetting protocols lead to qualitatively different steady states, highlighting the role of velocity distribution in resetting dynamics.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion induce directed motion and negative mobility in overdamped stochastic systems.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion and negative mobility in stochastic systems, which is relevant to transport in confined geometries.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion and reflecting boundaries, analyzing the no-flux condition and oblique reflection.
result: Boundary-induced drift emerges generically, and negative mobility (motion opposite to applied force) is observed under certain conditions.
conclusion: Boundary geometry alone can produce directed transport and negative mobility, with implications for nano-scale devices and biological systems.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, enabling entanglement certification without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photon pairs where conventional polarization analysis is impractical due to the need for Compton scattering.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry, deriving conditions under which polarization symmetry (equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses) holds if and only if the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is proven to be a necessary and sufficient condition for Bell states, providing a practical entanglement witness for Compton-scattered photons.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, though its applicability is limited to specific experimental scenarios.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena unique to open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation and compute topological invariants such as winding numbers.
result: They find that the system exhibits nonreciprocal dynamics and topological phases characterized by complex-energy winding numbers, with edge states appearing in certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work reveals a rich interplay between driving, dissipation, and topology, but the focus is on topological classification rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness (magic) measures for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using exact diagonalization or tensor network methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes of the binding-energy curve for H2 and other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, highlighting a new quantum resource in chemical systems.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins at high magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device applications, but the paper focuses on a specific experimental system without direct connection to information-theoretic or thermodynamic bounds.
method: The authors perform time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands to measure electron and nuclear spin temperatures after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower nuclear spin-mediated cooling, with the nuclear spin bath acting as a heat sink.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, which may be relevant for understanding thermalization in quantum devices but does not advance core information thermodynamics.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially when circuits are dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions significantly enhance the feasibility of classical simulation for near-Clifford circuits, which is relevant for quantum advantage experiments.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana bound states.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify promising platforms for Majorana-based qubits, but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation, enabling efficient estimation of noisy expectation values.
motivation: Understanding the impact of noise on quantum circuit complexity is crucial for near-term quantum advantage claims. The authors aim to characterize when noise enables classical simulation.
method: They develop a Pauli propagation technique that tracks the evolution of Pauli operators under noisy gates, leveraging the fact that local noise maps Pauli operators to mixtures of Paulis, leading to efficient classical algorithms.
result: They prove that for circuits with arbitrary local noise, the output expectation values can be computed in polynomial time on a classical computer, and provide explicit algorithms with rigorous runtime bounds.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise renders typical quantum circuits classically simulable, suggesting that quantum advantage requires very low noise levels or specific noise structures.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational approach that identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes, allowing the processor to operate on a reduced set of modes.
result: The method achieves near-constant hardware footprint regardless of the number of input modes, significantly reducing resource requirements.
conclusion: Variational supermode selection enables efficient multimode photonic processing, with potential applications in quantum information and sensing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and disconnected; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, showing how to derive and solve master equations.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, phase transitions, and large deviations in these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, such as photodoping and transient order, and discusses metastable superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements in various fields exceed them, prompting a need to understand why and how to exploit such effects.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, nonlinearity, or structural hierarchy, and shows how these can be engineered to achieve extreme material properties.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to surpass classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, opening avenues for novel high-performance materials.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System
authors: Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, And Jingyun Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, and Jingyun Fan

Extended, localized, and critical states form the three elementary classes of eigenstates underlying Anderson localization. While phases involving extended and localized states are widely studied, experimental realization of critical phases, particularly those where critical states coexist with othe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of five distinct localization phases in a 1D Floquet system, including critical phases.
motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize critical phases in disordered Floquet systems, which are less explored than extended and localized phases.
method: Using a photonic waveguide array with periodic driving and controlled disorder to observe different localization phases via wavefunction statistics.
result: Five distinct phases are identified: extended, localized, critical, and two mixed phases where critical states coexist with extended or localized states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the richness of localization phenomena in Floquet systems and provides a platform for studying critical phases.

title: Photodetection Of Squeezed Light: A Whittaker-Shannon Analysis
authors: Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, And J. E. Sipe
abstract:
Author(s): Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, and J. E. Sipe

The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition provides a temporally localized description of squeezed light, making it applicable in the continuous-wave limit and leading to a definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs at a time. We show examples of its usefulness by calculating quad…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063719] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Applies Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light in the continuous-wave limit, defining a temporally localized squeezing strength.
motivation: To provide a temporally localized description of squeezed light that is applicable in the continuous-wave limit, improving upon frequency-domain approaches.
method: Uses the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to represent squeezed light in the time domain and calculates quadrature variances.
result: Derives a definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs per time and demonstrates its utility with examples.
conclusion: The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition offers a useful time-domain framework for analyzing squeezed light, particularly for continuous-wave fields.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectra.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity is needed for quantum systems.
method: The paper proposes a quantum filtering algorithm that uses quantum signal processing to identify clusters and multiplicities.
result: The algorithm achieves improved efficiency for spectral analysis tasks.
conclusion: The method provides a practical quantum algorithm for eigenvalue problems.

title: Optical Tautochrone And Squeezing Dynamics In Nonuniform Lattices
authors: Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, And Konstantinos G. Makris
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, and Konstantinos G. Makris

We present exact analogies between the tautochrone problem of classical mechanics and the squeezed states of quantum optics to optical lattices. Both phenomena emerge in the same physical system, that of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings. Extension to two dimensions yields Lissajous-type tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
