tldr: This paper draws analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezed states in nonuniform optical lattices, demonstrating exact solutions for waveguide arrays.
motivation: To explore connections between classical mechanics and quantum optics in the context of optical lattices, and to find exact solutions for squeezing dynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings, deriving exact analogies to the tautochrone problem and extending to two-dimensional Lissajous-type trajectories.
result: They show that both the tautochrone and squeezing phenomena emerge in the same physical system, and provide exact solutions for the dynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals a deep connection between classical and quantum phenomena, but does not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, and is primarily a condensed matter physics result.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional quantum gases beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental realization in a Bose gas, using techniques from quantum field theory and cold atom physics.
result: Identifies a new class of critical states characterized by fractional Fermi seas, with distinct correlation properties.
conclusion: These exotic critical states extend the universality class of one-dimensional quantum systems and may have implications for quantum simulation.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent spin and valley dynamics in a van der Waals heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect, achieving subpicosecond control.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing in spin-and-valley-tronic devices.
method: Time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy and magneto-optical measurements on a MoSe2/CrSBr heterostructure.
result: Demonstrated subpicosecond coherent control of spin and valley pseudospin via the anomalous magnetic proximity effect, with long coherence times.
conclusion: The anomalous magnetic proximity effect enables ultrafast coherent manipulation of spin and valley degrees of freedom, promising for quantum technologies.

title: Biorthogonal Scattering And Generalized Unitarity In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, And Hee Chul Park
abstract:
Author(s): Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, and Hee Chul Park

We investigate the two-port scattering process in non-Hermitian dimer models via quantum measurements using external leads. We focus on two exemplary dimer models that preserve parity-time symmetry via spatial gain-loss balance and exhibit nonreciprocity due to directional hopping. The scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062213] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models with parity-time symmetry and nonreciprocity, focusing on biorthogonal scattering and generalized unitarity.
motivation: To understand scattering processes in non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant for open quantum systems and photonics, but not directly tied to the user's core interests.
method: The authors analyze two-port scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models using external leads, employing biorthogonal quantum mechanics and scattering matrix formalism.
result: They derive generalized unitarity relations and characterize scattering properties such as transmission and reflection in the presence of gain and loss.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for scattering in non-Hermitian systems but does not advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Distillation Of Topological Boundary States Via non-Hermitian Masking
authors: Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, And Gang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, and Gang Chen

Topological boundary states are a hallmark of topological phases, yet their direct detection remains challenging when they hybridize with bulk states or fail to form isolated in-gap modes. Here, we introduce a dynamical approach for directly distilling boundary-localized states in topological lattic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063514] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical method to distill topological boundary states using non-Hermitian masking in photonic lattices.
motivation: Topological boundary states are hard to detect when they hybridize with bulk states; the authors aim to directly distill them via a dynamical approach.
method: They introduce non-Hermitian masking (gain/loss) in a topological lattice and use time evolution to selectively amplify boundary-localized states.
result: The method successfully distills boundary states even when they are not isolated in-gap modes, demonstrated in a photonic platform.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian masking provides a practical tool for detecting topological boundary states, with potential applications in topological photonics.

title: Transport Scaling And Critical Tilt Effects In Disordered Two-dimensional Dirac Fermions
authors: Swadeepan Nanda And Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Swadeepan Nanda and Pavan Hosur

Two-dimensional (2D) Dirac fermions occur ubiquitously in condensed matter systems from topological phases to quantum critical points. Since the advent of topological semimetals, where the dispersion is often tilted around the band crossing where the Dirac fermion can appear, tilt has emerged as a k…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214203] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transport scaling and critical tilt effects in disordered two-dimensional Dirac fermions, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how tilt and disorder affect transport in 2D Dirac fermions is important for topological semimetals and quantum critical points.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to compute transport properties, likely including scaling analysis and disorder averaging.
result: They find that tilt modifies the critical exponents and transport scaling in the presence of disorder.
conclusion: Tilt is a crucial parameter for understanding transport in disordered Dirac systems, with implications for topological materials.

title: Interplay Of Quantum And Real-space Geometry In The Anomalous Landau Levels Of Singular Flat Bands
authors: Xuanyu Long And Feng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xuanyu Long and Feng Liu

The quantum geometry of the electronic states in momentum space, distinct from real-space structural geometry, has attracted increasing interest that has advanced our understanding of quantum phenomena. An important physical manifestation is the recent discovery of anomalous Landau level spreading $…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235119] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of quantum geometry and real-space geometry in anomalous Landau levels of singular flat bands.
motivation: To understand the physical manifestation of quantum geometry in momentum space and its relation to real-space structural geometry in flat band systems.
method: The authors analyze the quantum geometry of electronic states in singular flat bands and derive the anomalous Landau level spreading using theoretical calculations.
result: They find that the anomalous Landau level spreading is determined by the interplay of quantum and real-space geometry.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum geometry in flat bands and its observable consequences.

title: Three-dimensional Spin-orbital Liquids
authors: Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, And Maria Hermanns
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, and Maria Hermanns

Here, the authors introduce exactly solvable three-dimensional spin–orbital liquids that generalize Kitaev models using multiple Majorana flavors. They show that these systems realize a unifying landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and show how symmetry and flavor mixing control their splitting, stability, and topological transitions. This provides an organizing framework for gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235120] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces exactly solvable three-dimensional spin-orbital liquids generalizing Kitaev models, focusing on Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points.
motivation: To understand gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions, which are less explored than their two-dimensional counterparts.
method: The authors construct exactly solvable models using multiple Majorana flavors and analyze their band structures, topological features, and symmetry properties.
result: They find a unifying landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and show how symmetry and flavor mixing control their splitting, stability, and topological transitions.
conclusion: This provides an organizing framework for gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions.

title: Time-dependent Fluctuating Local Field Approach For The Description Of Correlated Fermions Dynamics
authors: L. D. Silakov, Ya. S. Lyakhova, And A. N. Rubtsov
abstract:
Author(s): L. D. Silakov, Ya. S. Lyakhova, and A. N. Rubtsov

We formulate a time-dependent Fluctuating Local Field (TD-FLF) method for correlated fermion dynamics, extending the stationary FLF approach. The wave function is approximated as an ensemble of noninteracting states subject to a classical fluctuating field, with dynamics encoded in the field's time-…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235121] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A time-dependent extension of the fluctuating local field method for simulating correlated fermion dynamics.
motivation: To describe the real-time dynamics of correlated fermionic systems beyond static approximations.
method: The wave function is approximated as an ensemble of noninteracting states subject to a classical fluctuating field, with dynamics encoded in the field's time-correlation function.
result: The method provides a computationally efficient approach to capture dynamical correlations in fermionic systems.
conclusion: The TD-FLF method offers a practical tool for studying non-equilibrium dynamics of correlated fermions, though its accuracy depends on the field fluctuation model.

title: Single-particle Dynamical Signature Of Topology Induced By Single Mode Cavities In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. de Filippis, And C. A. Perroni
abstract:
Author(s): F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. De Filippis, and C. A. Perroni

Witnessing and tracking topological phase transitions induced by interactions with the environment is a crucial challenge. Among the various experimental approaches to detect topological properties, the Mean Chiral Displacement (MCD) has emerged as a powerful bulk probe in one-dimensional chiral sys…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain induced by coupling to a single-mode cavity, using the mean chiral displacement as a probe.
motivation: To detect and track topological phase transitions induced by environmental interactions, which is a challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain coupled to a single-mode cavity, computing the mean chiral displacement to characterize topological properties.
result: They find that the cavity can induce topological phase transitions and that the mean chiral displacement serves as a dynamical signature of these transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a method to witness topology in open quantum systems using a bulk probe, relevant for cavity-QED setups.

title: Chiral Topological Superconductivity In Twisted Bilayer And Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene
authors: Kamalesh Bera, Tanay Nag, And Arijit Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Kamalesh Bera, Tanay Nag, and Arijit Saha

We present a theoretical investigation of the emergence of chiral topological superconductivity in small-angle twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) and twisted double bilayer graphene (tDBLG). Using the low-energy continuum model and incorporating spin-triplet [MATH] pairing in each graphene …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245418] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies chiral topological superconductivity in twisted bilayer and double bilayer graphene using a low-energy continuum model with spin-triplet pairing.
motivation: To understand the emergence of topological superconductivity in twisted graphene systems, which are of interest for fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: The authors employ a low-energy continuum model and incorporate spin-triplet pairing to analyze the electronic structure and topological properties.
result: They predict the existence of chiral topological superconductivity in both twisted bilayer and twisted double bilayer graphene.
conclusion: Twisted graphene systems can host chiral topological superconducting phases, offering a platform for studying Majorana modes and topological quantum computation.

title: Nonreciprocal Equilibrium Josephson Effect Of Arbitrary Periodicity From Poor Man's Majorana Zero Modes
authors: Panagiotis Kotetes, Mercè Roig, And Brian M. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Kotetes, Mercè Roig, and Brian M. Andersen

We show that the Josephson diode effect becomes possible when two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of pointlike magnetic adatoms are deposited on top of a Rashba superconductor. The degree of nonreciprocity is substantial when the arising Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound states approach zero energy. In …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241403] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a nonreciprocal Josephson diode effect using Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states from magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor.
motivation: To realize a Josephson diode with large nonreciprocity by engineering zero-energy bound states in a hybrid superconductor-magnetic system.
method: The authors theoretically study two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor, analyzing the Josephson current through the YSR bound states.
result: They find a substantial Josephson diode effect when YSR states approach zero energy, with nonreciprocity tunable by the coupling and magnetic configuration.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a platform for a nonreciprocal Josephson effect with arbitrary periodicity, relevant for superconducting diodes.

title: Periodic Dynamics In An Ising Chain With A Quadratic Transverse Field
authors: H. P. Zhang And Z. Song
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Zhang and Z. Song

A quadratic well plays a central role in a wide variety of modern physical theories and applications. In this work, we investigate many-body dynamics in a quadratic well, using an Ising chain as a paradigmatic example. In contrast to a uniform Ising chain, where the quantum phase transition is drive…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214313] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies many-body dynamics in an Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, focusing on periodic dynamics and quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how a quadratic well influences many-body dynamics in a spin chain, contrasting with uniform field behavior.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, examining time evolution and phase transitions.
result: The quadratic field leads to periodic dynamics and modifies the quantum phase transition compared to the uniform case.
conclusion: The quadratic transverse field introduces new dynamical features, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven quantum spin system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport, focusing on the effect of detuning the driving frequency.
motivation: To understand how detuning from the high-frequency regime affects the stability and properties of Floquet-induced chiral spin liquids, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and effective Hamiltonian approaches to analyze a periodically driven spin-1/2 system on a kagome lattice, varying the driving frequency.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous CSL phases, and detuning leads to a transition between different topological phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness and tunability of Floquet chiral spin liquids, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
authors: Yasuhiro Tada
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) for characterizing quantum many-body phases, extending validity to one-dimensional and higher-dimensional systems.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are used to identify gapped and gapless phases, but their validity beyond one dimension and in certain settings is not fully established.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the twist operator expectation value in various interacting quantum many-body models, including one-dimensional and higher-dimensional systems.
result: The study confirms the validity of the polarization index in one dimension and provides conditions for its extension to higher dimensions, though limitations are identified.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices are a useful diagnostic for quantum phases, but their applicability in higher dimensions requires careful consideration of system-specific details.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: To understand how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature, which is relevant for condensed matter systems with slow defect dynamics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model and analytical/numerical methods to analyze the effects of quenched disorder on topological transitions.
result: They find that quenched disorder can modify the nature of topological transitions, potentially leading to new phases or altered critical behavior.
conclusion: The presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder significantly impacts finite-temperature topological transitions, with implications for understanding disordered topological materials.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a classical computer.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum mechanics extends standard quantum theory to open systems with gain/loss, but self-consistent formulations are lacking.
method: The authors propose a formalism that ensures probability conservation via a time-dependent metric and emulate it using classical simulations.
result: They show that the formalism reproduces known non-Hermitian effects and can be efficiently simulated classically.
conclusion: The work provides a consistent framework for non-Hermitian quantum mechanics but does not directly connect to the user's research interests.

title: Update Of Hartree-Fock Theory For Hubbard-like Models
authors: E. Langmann And J. Lenells
abstract:
Author(s): E. Langmann and J. Lenells

We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitative errors in established condensed matter results.
motivation: Standard textbook Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard models yields qualitatively wrong results; an update is needed to correct the literature.
method: The authors reformulate restricted Hartree-Fock theory for Fermi Hubbard-like models, providing a corrected mathematical framework.
result: They show that previous results are incorrect and present corrected solutions for basic Hubbard model problems.
conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard textbook treatment for Hubbard-like models.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging standard assumptions.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced effects.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics and the connection to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep links to quantum circuit models.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods are limited to cold atoms. This work aims to extend such control to thermal gases.
method: Uses a thermal gas of atoms with a spatially structured pump to induce collective superfluorescence with controlled transverse modes.
result: Achieves cavity-free mode control of superfluorescence in a thermal gas, showing that collective radiation can be harnessed without cooling.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for light mode control in thermal gases, potentially useful for light sources and quantum optics.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), enabling ultracold atomic hydrogen production.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride and dissociating it offers a new route.
method: The authors laser-cool and magneto-optically trap calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules using a bichromatic force and a MOT configuration.
result: They successfully trap CaH molecules at microkelvin temperatures, demonstrating a viable precursor for ultracold hydrogen.
conclusion: This work opens a path to ultracold atomic hydrogen via dissociation of trapped CaH, with potential applications in quantum science.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand how vibrational excitations affect electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy or similar techniques.
result: Observation of electron bunching mediated by vibrational excitations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale transport.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems despite the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperatures, contradicting the conventional expectation.
conclusion: Critical fluctuations can stabilize long-range order in quasi-2D systems with short-range interactions.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a theoretical framework based on nonlinear response functions.
result: The method can access nonlinear quantum field dynamics and reveal features beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear dynamics in quantum many-body systems.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Efimov effect is a universal three-body phenomenon, but its observation in dipolar systems is challenging due to anisotropic interactions. This work aims to show that microwave shielding can restore universality.
method: Quantum-mechanical three-body calculations using realistic interaction potentials for shielded dipolar molecules.
result: Prediction of observable Efimov resonances and universal three-body parameters in the shielded regime.
conclusion: Microwave shielding enables Efimov physics in polar molecules, offering a new platform to study universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium, identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital angular momentum does not couple to magnetic fields, so a proper theoretical formulation is needed.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM via the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for OAM conservation.
result: They establish a consistent theory of magnon OAM at equilibrium, showing it is a well-defined physical quantity.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for understanding magnon OAM, which may impact spintronics and magnonics.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the core structure and elastic properties of skyrmion dislocations, revealing a topological phase transition.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and undergo a topological phase transition, leading to emergent elasticity.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into skyrmion lattice mechanics but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales-type lattice defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.
motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a candidate for topological quantum computation.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including mean-field theory or exact diagonalization, to study the Kitaev model with odd-sided plaquettes introduced by defects.
result: A finite density of defects leads to a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids at finite temperature, offering a new route to realize topological order in real materials.

title: Two Accelerated Mirrors In Opposite Rindler Wedges
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We investigate a quantum system consisting of two mirrors undergoing uniform acceleration in opposite directions and one or two stationary atoms localized in the right and left Rindler wedges, respectively. The system interacts with a scalar field described by plane-wave solutions in Rindler coordin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062615] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies two uniformly accelerated mirrors and stationary atoms in Rindler wedges interacting with a scalar field, focusing on quantum effects in accelerated frames.
motivation: To understand quantum field phenomena in non-inertial frames, particularly the interaction between accelerated boundaries and atoms.
method: Analytical calculations using plane-wave solutions in Rindler coordinates and quantum field theory.
result: The analysis yields insights into the dynamics of the system, such as radiation or entanglement properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of quantum effects in accelerated systems but does not directly address the user's research directions.

title: Stability Of Current-carrying States In Hard-core Bosons With Long-range Hopping On A Square Lattice
authors: Yoshihiro Yabuuchi And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshihiro Yabuuchi and Ippei Danshita

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the stability of superfluid currents in lattice systems with long-range interactions is important for condensed matter theory, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the Bose-Hubbard model with algebraically decaying hopping on a square lattice.
result: They find that current-carrying states become unstable above a critical current, with the stability region depending on the hopping exponent α.
conclusion: The work provides insights into current stability in long-range hopping systems but is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Properties Of Bose-Einstein Condensates With Altermagnetism
authors: Jia Wang, Zhao Liu, Xia-Ji Liu, And Hui Hu
abstract:

We investigate a weakly interacting two-component Bose-Einstein condensate in the miscible regime in the presence of altermagnetism, i.e., a collinear and globally compensated magnetic order that breaks spin-rotation symmetry while maintaining zero net magnetization. Within Bogoliubov theory, we der…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063316] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Bose-Einstein condensates with altermagnetism using Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: To understand the properties of a two-component BEC in the presence of altermagnetic order, which breaks spin-rotation symmetry but has zero net magnetization.
method: Bogoliubov theory is applied to a weakly interacting two-component BEC in the miscible regime with altermagnetism.
result: Derivation of excitation spectra and other properties of the altermagnetic BEC.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of altermagnetism in a BEC system, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. However, optical loss, which reduces the entanglement in the system, can render GBS results classically simulable. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062433] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonlinear photonic architecture using optical parametric amplifiers to mitigate loss in Gaussian boson sampling.
motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the results classically simulable, undermining claims of quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce optical parametric amplification networks within the boson sampling setup to counteract loss and restore non-classical correlations.
result: The proposed architecture improves the robustness of GBS against loss, potentially preserving quantum computational advantage.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to boost GBS performance in the presence of loss.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, and Jie-Yun Yan

A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed to achieve highly efficient optical bistability. By exploiting the conjugate topological edge state supported by the CTPC, the structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold, reaching the level of a few microwatts per meter in …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063519] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced optical bistability in conjugate topological photonic crystals using topological edge states.
motivation: Optical bistability is important for all-optical switching and memory, but conventional structures require high thresholds. Topological photonic crystals offer robust edge states that could lower the threshold.
method: A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed by combining two topologically distinct photonic crystals. The nonlinear optical response is analyzed using coupled-mode theory and finite-difference time-domain simulations.
result: The CTPC exhibits a bistability threshold reduced to a few microwatts per meter, significantly lower than conventional designs, due to the strong field confinement of the topological edge state.
conclusion: Conjugate topological photonic crystals provide a promising platform for low-power optical bistability and all-optical signal processing.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient
authors: Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, And Le Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, and Le Luo

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; faster cooling is needed for practical quantum simulation and many-body physics experiments.
method: The authors apply a magnetic field gradient to tilt the optical dipole trap, which lowers the potential barrier and increases the evaporation rate while maintaining high phase-space density.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling times compared to standard evaporation, reaching quantum degeneracy more rapidly.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, enabling more efficient experiments in strongly correlated quantum systems.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing effects in a laboratory setting.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing using analog models and to design optical devices that mimic curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling and simulations of light propagation in an analog black hole system.
result: They observe optical echoes and analyze their properties, demonstrating analog gravitational lensing.
conclusion: Analog black holes can serve as testbeds for gravitational lensing phenomena and inspire novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, proposing optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to divergent heating rates in collapse models; the smearing distribution is arbitrary, so the authors seek an optimal choice to minimize energy nonconservation.
method: The authors analyze the heating rate as a functional of the smearing distribution and derive conditions for optimal smearing that minimizes diffusion.
result: An optimal smearing function is identified that reduces the heating rate to a finite, minimal value, providing a testable prediction for collapse models.
conclusion: Optimal smearing can mitigate the unphysical divergence in heating, making collapse models more consistent and experimentally constrained.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, and Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214435] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent fields can induce topological phases in frustrated magnets with spatial inversion symmetry.
method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identifies conditions for topological phase transitions and characterizes the resulting phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields can control topological phases in frustrated magnets, offering a route to manipulate quantum materials.

title: Hall Anomaly In The Mixed State Of type-II Superconductors: Evidence For Vacancies Within Vortex Lattice Domains
authors: Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, and Ping Ao

Despite numerous recent studies on the Hall anomaly following the discovery of cuprate superconductivity, its origin remains contentious. We demonstrate—without invoking adjustable parameters—that a previously proposed mechanism, in which vacancies form within vortex lattice domains, provides a comp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214513] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains to explain the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors, without adjustable parameters.
motivation: The origin of the Hall anomaly in cuprate superconductors remains contentious, and the authors aim to validate a previously proposed mechanism.
method: The authors demonstrate that vacancies forming within vortex lattice domains can explain the Hall anomaly, using a parameter-free model.
result: The model successfully reproduces the Hall anomaly without adjustable parameters, providing evidence for the vacancy mechanism.
conclusion: The vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains is a viable explanation for the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.

title: Exact Mobility Edges And Hidden Self-duality In non-Hermitian Quasiperiodic Network Models
authors: San-Ren He, Jing Fan, Lin Li, Rui Wang, Dong-Hui Xu, And Zhen-Hua Wang
abstract:

The determination of the mobility edge (ME)—the critical energy threshold separating extended and localized quantum states—remains a central challenge in the study of Anderson transitions, particularly within complex non-Hermitian systems where conventional Hermitian techniques often fail. While the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224205] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact mobility edges in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network models, revealing hidden self-duality.
motivation: Determining mobility edges in non-Hermitian systems is challenging; the authors aim to find exact solutions using self-duality.
method: They analyze a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network model and identify a hidden self-duality that allows exact calculation of mobility edges.
result: Exact expressions for mobility edges are derived, showing transitions between extended and localized states.
conclusion: The work provides a method to analytically determine mobility edges in certain non-Hermitian systems, advancing understanding of Anderson transitions.

title: Creation Of Domain-wall Skyrmions In Chiral Magnets With Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Dynamics And Demagnetization
authors: Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Yuki Amari, And Muneto Nitta
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Yuki Amari, and Muneto Nitta

Absorption of an isolated bulk magnetic skyrmion into an empty domain wall in a chiral ferromagnetic system is studied using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without the demagnetization effect taken into account. The full phase diagram of creation versus repulsion or annihilation is map…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224425] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the absorption of magnetic skyrmions into domain walls in chiral magnets using Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, mapping the phase diagram of creation, repulsion, or annihilation.
motivation: Understanding the interaction between skyrmions and domain walls is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on classical micromagnetic simulations without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically solve the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without demagnetization effects to simulate skyrmion-domain wall interactions.
result: A full phase diagram of creation versus repulsion or annihilation is mapped out for isolated bulk magnetic skyrmions absorbed into an empty domain wall.
conclusion: The work provides insights into skyrmion dynamics in chiral magnets, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hund's Coupling Governed Orbital-selective Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{K}}_{x}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, and Zhi-Xun Shen

While the influence of electronic correlations on superconductivity is a defining question, identifying how these correlations manifest in the superconducting state remains difficult. Furthermore, in multiorbital systems, correlations driven by Hund’s coupling can differentiate the behavior of individual orbitals, and how such orbital selectivity governs superconducting pairing has remained largely unexplored experimentally. Here, the authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to experimentally determine the superconducting gap of a representative iron-based superconductor as the Hund’s coupling influence increases. They find increased correlation diminishes the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective way, suggesting that Hund’s coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224517] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ARPES to study orbital-selective superconductivity in Ba1-xKxFe2As2, finding that Hund's coupling governs the suppression of the superconducting gap in a correlation-dependent manner.
motivation: To understand how electronic correlations, particularly Hund's coupling, influence superconductivity in multiorbital systems, which remains experimentally unexplored.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the superconducting gap in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 as a function of doping, which tunes the strength of Hund's coupling.
result: Increased correlations due to Hund's coupling lead to an orbital-selective reduction of the superconducting gap, with the most correlated orbitals showing the largest suppression.
conclusion: Hund's coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors, providing a mechanism for orbital-selective superconductivity.

title: Fermi Surface And Topology Of The Multiband Superconductor BeAu
authors: Riccardo Vocaturo, Klaus Koepernik, Dániel Varjas, Oleg Janson, Maia G. Vergniory, And Jeroen van Den Brink

The chiral material BeAu was recently identified as a multiband type-I superconductor with a critical temperature of 3.2 K. As a member of the B20 crystal family (space group [MATH]), its band structure hosts multifold fermions at high-symmetry points, unpaired WPs, and even nodal surfaces. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224518] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure and topological properties of the superconductor BeAu using DFT and symmetry analysis.
motivation: To understand the superconducting and topological properties of BeAu, a multiband type-I superconductor with chiral structure.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and symmetry analysis of band structure, including multifold fermions, Weyl points, and nodal surfaces.
result: BeAu hosts multifold fermions, unpaired Weyl points, and nodal surfaces; its Fermi surface is complex with multiple bands.
conclusion: BeAu is a promising platform for studying the interplay between superconductivity and topology.

title: Three-body Fermi-liquid Corrections For Andreev Transport Through Quantum Dots
authors: Akira Oguri, Masashi Hashimoto, And Yoshimichi Teratani
abstract:
Author(s): Akira Oguri, Masashi Hashimoto, and Yoshimichi Teratani

We study crossed Andreev reflection occurring in quantum dots connected to one superconducting lead and two normal leads at low temperatures [MATH]. Specifically, we derive an exact formula for the conductance up to order [MATH] in the large-superconducting-gap limit, which is expressed in terms of …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235416] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies three-body Fermi-liquid corrections to Andreev transport through quantum dots with superconducting and normal leads.
motivation: To understand the effect of electron interactions on crossed Andreev reflection in quantum dot systems.
method: Derives an exact formula for conductance up to order T^2 in the large-superconducting-gap limit using Fermi-liquid theory.
result: The conductance formula is expressed in terms of the local Fermi-liquid parameters of the quantum dot.
conclusion: Three-body correlations play a significant role in Andreev transport, providing corrections beyond the two-body approximation.

title: Nonlinear Topological Edge States, Topological Gap Solitons, And Self-induced Topological Edge States In Nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Circuit Lattices
authors: Rujiang Li, Wencai Wang, Xiangyu Kong, Ce Shang, Yongtao Jia, Gui-Geng Liu, Huibin Tao, Ying Liu, And Baile Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Rujiang Li, Wencai Wang, Xiangyu Kong, Ce Shang, Yongtao Jia, Gui-Geng Liu, Huibin Tao, Ying Liu, and Baile Zhang

Topological edge states typically arise at the boundaries of topologically nontrivial structures or at interfaces between regions with different topological invariants. When topological systems are extended into the nonlinear regime, linear topological edge states bifurcate into nonlinear counterpar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214310] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear topological edge states and gap solitons in SSH circuit lattices, focusing on nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend topological edge states into the nonlinear regime and explore their bifurcations and self-induced counterparts.
method: Theoretical analysis and circuit lattice experiments on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with Kerr nonlinearity.
result: Nonlinear topological edge states bifurcate from linear ones, and topological gap solitons and self-induced topological edge states are observed.
conclusion: Nonlinearity enriches topological phenomena, but the work is primarily in classical nonlinear optics and topological photonics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Magnonic Properties Of Hematite α-${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: A Combined ab Initio And Atomistic Spin Dynamics Study
authors: Shanshan Hu, Ziyang Li, Liya Qiao, Yuzhong Zhang, Zongzhi Zhang, And Yaowen Liu

Altermagnets are promising candidates for next-generation low-dissipation magnonic devices due to their ultrafast spin dynamics and chiral splitting magnon bands. Hematite [MATH], a widely recognized altermagnet with an ultralow damping constant, subterahertz ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214432] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnonic properties of hematite using ab initio and atomistic spin dynamics, focusing on altermagnetic spin dynamics and magnon bands.
motivation: Altermagnets like hematite are promising for low-dissipation magnonic devices due to ultrafast spin dynamics and chiral magnon bands, but their magnonic properties need detailed theoretical characterization.
method: The authors combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with atomistic spin dynamics simulations to compute magnon dispersion, damping, and spin-wave spectra.
result: They obtain magnon band structures showing chiral splitting and ultralow damping, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Hematite exhibits altermagnetic magnonic features suitable for spintronic applications, and the combined ab initio and spin dynamics approach is effective for predicting magnon properties.

title: Double-twisted Surface Spectrum From Hybridized Majorana Kramers Pairs And Wallpaper Fermions
authors: Kaito Yoda And Ai Yamakage
abstract:

We theoretically investigate the superconducting surface states of topological nonsymmorphic crystalline insulators with wallpaper fermions, which are surface quasiparticles protected by a wallpaper group [MATH] symmetry, based on a tight-binding model for the space group [MATH] (No. 127). A symmet…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224515] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconducting surface states of topological nonsymmorphic crystalline insulators with wallpaper fermions, focusing on the double-twisted surface spectrum from hybridized Majorana Kramers pairs.
motivation: To understand the surface states of topological nonsymmorphic crystalline insulators and the role of wallpaper fermions in generating novel superconducting surface spectra.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model for a specific space group and analyze the surface states, including the hybridization of Majorana Kramers pairs.
result: They find a double-twisted surface spectrum arising from the interplay of wallpaper fermions and Majorana Kramers pairs.
conclusion: The work reveals new features in the surface spectrum of topological nonsymmorphic insulators, relevant for understanding topological superconductivity.

title: Dirac Quantum Criticality In Twisted Double Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Jan Biedermann And Lukas Janssen
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Biedermann and Lukas Janssen

Quantum criticality involving Dirac fermions has long been studied theoretically but has remained difficult to access experimentally. Here, the authors predict that twisted double bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, such as WSe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245123] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Dirac quantum criticality in twisted double bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, a condensed matter system.
motivation: To find experimentally accessible platforms for Dirac quantum criticality, which has been theoretically studied but hard to realize.
method: Theoretical analysis of twisted double bilayer TMDs, tuning twist angle or uniaxial pressure to access a semimetal-to-insulator transition.
result: The transition is continuous and governed by Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg criticality with emergent Lorentz symmetry.
conclusion: Twisted double bilayer TMDs host a Dirac quantum critical point, offering a new platform to study quantum criticality.

title: Tunable Optical Spin Hall Effect In An Open Cavity
authors: Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen

The optical spin Hall effect (OSHE), resulting from photonic spin-orbit coupling, has become a pivotal phenomenon in nanophotonics. tldr: This paper demonstrates a tunable optical spin Hall effect in an open cavity, enabling broadband and material-independent control of photonic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: The optical spin Hall effect is important for nanophotonics, but existing platforms are limited to specific materials like liquid crystals. A more general, tunable platform is desired.
method: The authors use an open cavity design with a patterned mirror to achieve tunable spin-orbit coupling, and experimentally demonstrate the effect.
result: They achieve a tunable optical spin Hall effect with broadband operation, independent of the cavity material.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for controlling photonic spin-orbit coupling, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Edge Spin Galvanic Effect In Altermagnets
authors: L. E. Golub

[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220404] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.

motivation: To explore spin-charge conversion phenomena in altermagnets, a class of magnetic materials with unique spin splitting.
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and scattering theory to model edge transport in altermagnets.
result: Prediction of an edge spin galvanic effect sensitive to edge orientation and Néel vector, and a pure spin edge photocurrent convertible to electric current by a magnetic field.
conclusion: Altermagnets can host edge spin galvanic effects, offering new routes for spintronic applications.

title: Dimerization In The Ising Ladder With Four-spin Plaquette Interaction Induced By A Random Transverse Field
authors: Wescley Luiz de Souza, Paulo H. L. Martins, And Érica de Mello Silva
abstract:

The current interest in dimerization spans several scientific areas. In quantum computation, chains of spin dimers contribute as a medium of coherent quantum state transfer, which is essential for the storage and processing of quantum information. In biophysics, molecular dimers are widely used to u…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214427] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dimerization in an Ising ladder with four-spin plaquette interaction under a random transverse field, focusing on the effects of disorder on the dimerized phase.
motivation: Dimerization is relevant for quantum state transfer in quantum computation and for biophysics, but the paper's primary focus is on the statistical mechanics of a disordered quantum spin system.
method: The authors use a quantum Monte Carlo method to simulate the Ising ladder with four-spin interactions and a random transverse field, analyzing the dimer order parameter and correlation functions.
result: They find that the random transverse field can induce or enhance dimerization, and they map out the phase diagram as a function of disorder strength and temperature.
conclusion: Disorder can stabilize dimer order in the Ising ladder, which may have implications for understanding quantum state transfer in disordered media.

title: Polaron-mediated Anisotropic Exchange In Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:

Two-dimensional (2D) magnets offer a rich platform for exploring emergent spin phenomena due to their unique and diverse magnetic properties. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 214428] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-mediated anisotropic exchange in 2D magnets, focusing on defect engineering and charge doping to control magnetic properties.
motivation: To understand and control emergent spin phenomena in 2D magnets through external manipulation such as defects and doping.
method: The authors likely use first-principles calculations or model Hamiltonians to study the effect of polarons on magnetic exchange interactions.
result: They find that polaron formation can mediate anisotropic exchange interactions, offering a route to tune magnetism in 2D materials.
conclusion: Polaron-mediated exchange provides a mechanism for controlling magnetic order in 2D magnets, relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Anomalous Quantum Oscillations In InAs/GaSb Quantum Wells
authors: Xinlong Du, Chao Wang, Bo Ying, And Juntao Song

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214429] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the effect of spin-orbit coupling on anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells, a condensed matter physics topic without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how spin-orbit coupling influences anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells, which are relevant for topological insulators.
method: Theoretical analysis comparing different cases of spin-orbit coupling strength in a model of InAs/GaSb quantum wells.
result: Spin-orbit coupling suppresses oscillations in the clean case but enhances them in the presence of disorder.
conclusion: The interplay of spin-orbit coupling and disorder is crucial for understanding anomalous quantum oscillations in these systems.

The metallic kagome compound [MATH] has attracted attention as a candidate platform where geometric frustration and itinerant electrons may cooperate to stabilize a quantum-disordered magnetic ground state. Here, we combine bulk thermod…

motivation: To understand how geometric frustration and itinerant electrons in a kagome lattice may lead to a quantum-disordered magnetic ground state.
method: Combination of bulk thermodynamic measurements, NMR, and theoretical analysis to characterize the magnetic properties.
result: Evidence for emergent spin-singlet pairing and a quantum-disordered state in the kagome metal.
conclusion: The compound serves as a platform for studying frustration-driven quantum magnetism, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics angle.

title: Orbital Altermagnetism On The Kagome Lattice And Possible Application To ${A\mathrm{V}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$
authors: Anzumaan R. Chakraborty, Fan Yang, Turan Birol, And Rafael M. Fernandes

motivation: To explore altermagnetic states in lattices with odd sublattice count and connect to kagome materials.
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and mean-field calculations on a kagome lattice model.
result: Identifies orbital altermagnetic order and discusses its possible realization in AV3Sb5 compounds.
conclusion: Orbital altermagnetism is a viable concept in kagome lattices, with potential material candidates.

title: Superconductivity In The Pressure-amorphized Topological Insulator $\mathrm{Cr}{\mathrm{P}}_{4}$
authors: Chutong Zhang, Xiangzhuo Xing, Na Zuo, Bowen Zheng, Bin Li, Jiajia Feng, Xiaolei Yi, Yan Meng, Xiaoran Zhang, Bingchao Yang, Chao Wang, Xin Chen, Yongsheng Zhang, Xiaofeng Xu, And Xiaobing Liu

motivation: To explore novel superconductivity in Cr-based transition-metal compounds and understand the relationship between superconductivity, magnetism, and nontrivial band topology.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying several stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems by analyzing a general class of Lévy walk models.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for variable speed generalized Lévy walks and derive exact expressions for the decomposition of the mean squared displacement into ballistic, diffusive, and other components.
result: They obtain a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion process, showing how different speed and waiting time distributions contribute to the overall dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a unified understanding of anomalous diffusion in Lévy walks, which may be useful for modeling transport in complex systems.

title: Spectral Properties Of non-Hermitian Real Random Matrices With Long-range Correlations

tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices with long-range correlations, focusing on deviations from the circular law.
motivation: Understanding how long-range correlations affect eigenvalue distributions in non-Hermitian random matrices, which is a topic in random matrix theory.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the radial eigenvalue density for real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as the correlation exponent decreases, with the radial density decaying faster than the circular law prediction.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter the spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices, leading to new universality classes.

title: Emergent Metastable Behavior In A Resource-constrained Network Of Exclusion Processes
authors: Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, And Arvind Kumar Gupta

method: They analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and resource constraints.
result: They find emergent metastable states and characterize their properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states in complex networks.

method: Numerical simulations and stability analysis of the 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole and azimuthal modulation.
result: Existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on driving amplitude, inner radius, and azimuthal modulation.
