[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and discrete Ricci curvature provides a geometric tool to capture connection patterns.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and information entropy optimization to detect communities.
result: The method effectively identifies community structures in complex networks, as demonstrated on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a novel geometric perspective for community detection, leveraging curvature and entropy.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic mechanical response, but the microscopic origin of aging in these systems is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, using statistical mechanics to study the dynamics of sticker clustering.
result: They find that entropic effects cause stickers to cluster over time, leading to a gradual increase in network connectivity and a corresponding aging of the material properties.
conclusion: The model explains aging in biocondensates as a result of entropic clustering, providing a physical mechanism for the observed viscoelastic behavior.

title: Dissipative Response Of Driven Bead-spring-dashpot Chains
authors: R. Kailasham
abstract:
Author(s): R. Kailasham

The work dissipated in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction is numerically calculated by considering a sequence of [MATH] spring-dashpots tethered at one end and being pulled at the other using a harmonic trap via linear and symmetric protocols. The variation of the dissipation with the chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065408] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the dissipated work in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction using a bead-spring-dashpot model.
motivation: Understanding dissipation in driven polymer chains is important for polymer physics and biophysics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors simulate a sequence of spring-dashpots tethered at one end and pulled by a harmonic trap using linear and symmetric protocols, computing the work dissipated.
result: The variation of dissipation with chain length and pulling protocol is characterized numerically.
conclusion: The study provides insights into dissipative response of polymer chains but remains within classical soft matter physics.

title: Controlling The Glass Transition Through Active Fluctuating Interactions
authors: Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, And Thibault Bertrand
abstract:
Author(s): Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, and Thibault Bertrand

Fluctuating pairwise interactions are understood to drive fluidlike states in dense biological systems. These states find a broad range of functionalities, such as directing growth during morphogenesis and forming aggregates with heightened mechanical response. However, a tractable model capturing t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062102] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active fluctuating interactions control the glass transition in dense biological systems.
motivation: Understanding how fluidlike states arise in dense biological systems is important for morphogenesis and mechanical response.
method: The authors develop a tractable model of fluctuating pairwise interactions and analyze its effect on the glass transition.
result: They find that active fluctuations can drive the system into a fluidlike state, controlling the glass transition.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of active interactions in biological materials.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric linearization principle, providing a dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in complex systems, but a consistent dynamical foundation is lacking.
method: The authors introduce a linearization principle at the dynamical level, leading to a geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations.
result: The derived equations describe anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions, unifying various nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations under a geometric framework.
conclusion: The linearization principle offers a geometric origin for nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, providing a consistent dynamical foundation for complex systems.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times in bosonic systems.
motivation: Traditional path integral Monte Carlo methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between multiple replicas at different temperatures to improve sampling efficiency.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measurements in continuous-space PIMC simulations.
conclusion: The exchange Monte Carlo approach is effective for accelerating PIMC simulations of bosonic systems at finite temperature.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics arguments to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds that the critical temperature is bounded above by a universal number determined by the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. Inspired by metapopulation models from ecology, we study opinion formation using a network-based approach in which nodes represent communities of i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion formation using a network-based metapopulation model, focusing on spatial pattern formation and diversity preservation.
motivation: Understanding how spatial organization and network structure influence opinion diversity in complex social systems.
method: A network model where nodes represent communities of individuals, with diffusion-driven dynamics inspired by ecological metapopulation models.
result: The model exhibits pattern formation and can preserve diversity under certain conditions.
conclusion: Spatial structure and network topology are key factors in maintaining opinion diversity.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws.
motivation: To understand how physical constraints affect learning dynamics and catastrophic forgetting in physical neural networks.
method: The authors use differentiable resistor networks as a model system, where learning is implemented by adjusting resistor values under Kirchhoff's laws.
result: They observe that sequential learning leads to catastrophic forgetting, similar to artificial neural networks, but with unique features due to physical constraints.
conclusion: Physical learning systems face similar challenges as artificial ones, and understanding these can inform the design of more robust physical learning machines.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: They included correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations to model the effect of phonon edge modes.
result: The simulations account for the observed enhanced vibrations, confirming the presence of localized phonon edge states.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes are responsible for the enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of MoS2, providing insight into edge effects in 2D materials.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence and emergent self-attention.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models to explain emergent attention mechanisms in biological and artificial systems.
method: The authors introduce a coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamical system with a Lyapunov function and analyze fixed points under an entropy-regularized replicator equation.
result: The model converges globally and exhibits self-attention-like behavior at fixed points, linking associative memory to attention.
conclusion: Astrocyte-gated dynamics can give rise to attention mechanisms, suggesting a biological basis for self-attention in neural computation.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network methodology that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems that were previously intractable with conventional techniques.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a viable route to study spectral properties of complex moiré systems.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Observation of an amplitudelike mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for studying macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying collective modes is key to understanding their physics.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitudelike mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for collective excitations in excitonic insulators, advancing understanding of their condensed phase.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore the analogy between the Frenkel line and the pseudogap.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities and response functions near critical endpoints in both classical and electronic fluids, using theoretical models and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They identify a line analogous to the Frenkel line in the electronic system, associated with the pseudogap phase, and show similarities in the behavior of thermodynamic maxima.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified perspective on critical phenomena in classical and quantum fluids, suggesting that the pseudogap can be understood as a manifestation of the Frenkel line in electronic systems.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: Quantum chemistry calculations on near-term quantum devices are limited by noise and qubit count; classical methods like configuration interaction are accurate but expensive. Combining both can leverage quantum resources to reduce classical cost.
method: The algorithm uses a quantum computer to prepare an approximate ground state and measure importance of configurations (determinants), then classically diagonalizes the Hamiltonian in the subspace of selected configurations.
result: The method achieves accurate energies with fewer configurations than standard classical selection, and is robust to noise on quantum devices.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction is a promising hybrid approach for quantum chemistry on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, balancing accuracy and resource requirements.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a mathematical model of an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine and shows its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To develop a physically implementable model of slime mold-inspired optimization that achieves high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors propose a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is shown to be equivalent to recurrent neural networks, enabling analysis of its dynamics and optimization capabilities.
conclusion: The amoeba-inspired machine can be understood as a type of recurrent neural network, bridging biological inspiration and neural computation.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules, focusing on radiation pressure forces from dark states.
motivation: Understanding how to trap and cool molecules is important for precision measurements and quantum science, but the paper is primarily about atomic/molecular physics and laser cooling techniques.
method: The authors analyze a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap with two frequency components and opposite circular polarizations, identifying a dark state mechanism that generates a restoring force.
result: They show that when Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference, a state is dark to one beam but not the other, producing a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.
conclusion: The identified mechanism explains trapping and cooling in such setups, but the work is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum-enhanced T-stochastic Neighbor Embedding For High-dimensional Data Visualization
authors: Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, And Song Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, and Song Lin

t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that preserves local similarity by matching probability distributions between high- and low-dimensional spaces. Owing to its ability to capture complex manifold structures, t-SNE has become a widely…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023265] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced version of t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization using quantum amplitude estimation and Grover's search.
motivation: Classical t-SNE is computationally expensive for large datasets; quantum algorithms may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that accelerates the computation of pairwise similarities and gradient descent steps in t-SNE using amplitude estimation and Grover's search.
result: The quantum t-SNE achieves a quadratic speedup in the number of data points and dimensions compared to classical t-SNE.
conclusion: Quantum computing can enhance nonlinear dimensionality reduction, but practical implementation requires fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, and Nicolás Morales-Durán

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials is crucial for realizing topological phases.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation to study the effect of Berry curvature inhomogeneity on many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the many-body gap and can drive a transition from fractional Chern insulator to charge density wave.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor destabilizing fractional Chern insulators, explaining experimental observations in moiré materials.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: Efficient simulation of active matter systems with many particles requires algorithms that handle steric interactions without time-step discretization errors.
method: The kinetic event-chain algorithm extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian particles, using event-driven dynamics for hard-core collisions.
result: The algorithm correctly reproduces motility-induced phase separation and shows improved efficiency over standard Brownian dynamics for high densities.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm is a promising tool for simulating dense active matter systems with hard-core interactions.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
authors: Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, And Romain Fleury
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, and Romain Fleury

Radiation forces and torques enable the manipulation of objects with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. Yet, harnessing them in complex scattering media remains a formidable challenge, especially when multiple objects must be controlled under competing objectives. Here, we demonstrate that sound or…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023254] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles in complex scattering media using acoustic tweezers.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects in scattering media is challenging due to competing objectives and complex wave propagation.
method: The authors use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to simultaneously trap and manipulate multiple particles with acoustic waves in a scattering environment.
result: They achieve simultaneous trapping and independent control of multiple particles, demonstrating multiobjective tweezing in a complex medium.
conclusion: The approach extends wave-based manipulation to complex media, enabling applications in biomedical and microfluidic systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere regularization, which replaces the continuous sphere with a finite-dimensional matrix algebra, to simulate fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They demonstrate that the fuzzy sphere can accurately capture the critical properties of free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and observe emergent supersymmetry in certain interacting models.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and the emergent supersymmetry suggests deeper connections between noncommutative geometry and quantum field theory.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superstructures, which could enable new ways to manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, thermodynamic measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2 and identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are discovered, and a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures is established.
conclusion: The work provides a blueprint for engineering spin textures in moiré materials, with potential applications in information storage and processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand whether topological magnon gaps survive at finite temperatures, which is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures, likely using many-body perturbation theory or spin-wave theory.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic arguments.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the paper aims to provide a general method using physical principles.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical constraints to infer causal links from observed dynamics in networks.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The physics-informed approach offers a powerful tool for causal inference in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting diodes, which is important for low-dissipation electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for realizing time-reversal symmetric superconducting diodes, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers near topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems by engineering anyonic exciton condensates.
method: Theoretical analysis using field theory and numerical methods to study the phase diagram and critical properties of quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables robust anyonic exciton superfluidity with unique properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for realizing anyonic superfluids, advancing the understanding of topological phases.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the frustrated kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits exotic magnetic behavior.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic order and critical exponents.
result: The system undergoes a phase transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and the ground state shows hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The kagome ice compound HoAgGe provides a realization of three-dimensional XY criticality and hosts a ground state with broken time-reversal symmetry, relevant to frustrated magnetism.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: The authors perform magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, on twisted bilayer WSe2 devices under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: They observe a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstrate electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall states and provides a method for controlling magnetic order via electric fields.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and their critical behavior at the liquid-vapor transition is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical exponents and scaling behavior of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-gas critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness (suppressed fluctuations) yet high susceptibility at the critical point, deviating from ordinary critical opalescence.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform systems, relevant to understanding phase transitions in correlated disordered materials.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize scattering and radiative loss.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures to observe gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of spin-dependent electron focusing and a ballistic spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can support coherent spin transport and spin control through electron optics, promising for spintronics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on the structural and dielectric properties of a specific condensed matter system.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering phenomena; understanding the dipolar nematic state may clarify their unusual dielectric response.
method: The authors likely use experimental techniques (e.g., dielectric spectroscopy, neutron scattering) or theoretical modeling to characterize the nematic ordering.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic phase and describe its properties, possibly linking it to the relaxor behavior.
conclusion: The dipolar nematic state is a key feature of relaxor ferroelectrics, with implications for understanding their physics.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: Increasing activity can counterintuitively reduce the solid's active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The percolation threshold governs the macroscopic active response, leading to a 'more is less' effect.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end implementation on current quantum hardware.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that implements the Hadamard test and controlled unitary operations to evaluate the Jones polynomial, and they run it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the feasibility of the algorithm on near-term devices.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the resources required for quantum advantage in topological computation.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose target states into a sequence of elementary operations, including photon catalysis, linear optics, and measurements.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a universal and efficient recipe for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics experiments.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome lattice materials, analyzing electronic structure, many-body effects, and observed phenomena.
result: Identifies key mechanisms including sublattice interference, spin-orbit coupling, and frustration leading to topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and exotic orders.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for studying correlated and topological physics, with potential for new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: Spin glasses are a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics has broad applications.
method: The paper reviews experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: It highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation in advancing the field.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with implications for many physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but this review does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials like α-RuCl3.
result: Summarizes progress in identifying Kitaev spin liquid candidates and their chiral edge modes.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of condensed matter physics, but the paper is not aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze simultaneous recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for predicting neural activity, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion, a nonradiative photophysical process, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key process in molecular photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings can aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting devices.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current theoretical methods and identifies open challenges.
conclusion: Further development of theoretical methods is needed to accurately describe internal conversion in complex systems, with potential impact on photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum dynamics.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior, but the field is still developing; further research is needed for quantum applications.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the Standard Model, such as exotic boson-mediated spin-dependent forces that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements and symmetry tests.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing quantum many-body physics in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions using atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
motivation: To explore quantum phenomena in nonstandard geometries that cannot be realized in conventional Euclidean lattices, enabling simulation of topological condensed matter and gravitational models.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for engineering synthetic quantum matter in fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional geometries across atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
result: Summarizes recent progress in realizing exotic geometries and discusses emergent phenomena such as topological states and analogies to gravity.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential for simulating fundamental physics, but it remains largely disconnected from the user's core interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects like decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts to detect gravity-induced decoherence, collapse, and entanglement between massive particles.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art experiments and theories, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of Berry curvature in generating nonlinear Hall effects without external magnetic fields.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 under an in-plane magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
result: A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism involving the Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effects in nonmagnetic topological materials, with potential applications in rectification and frequency doubling.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Observation of switchable chiral magnons in altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: To provide unambiguous evidence of chirality in split magnon bands of altermagnets, a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: Polarized inelastic neutron scattering on MnTe single crystals.
result: First direct observation of chiral magnon bands in an altermagnet.
conclusion: Confirms theoretical predictions of chirality in altermagnets, advancing understanding of magnetic materials.

title: Crystal-Field-Tuned Spin-Flip Luminescence In ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, And Abhay Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, and Abhay Shukla

Layered magnetic materials provide the opportunity for fundamental investigations of magnetism in the two-dimensional limit. [MATH], a prototype member of this family, is antiferromagnetic below 155 K and exhibits sharp photoluminescence associated with a transition between a triplet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236401] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal-field-tuned spin-flip luminescence in the layered antiferromagnet NiPS3, focusing on its optical and magnetic properties.

method: Photoluminescence spectroscopy combined with crystal field tuning, likely through external perturbations or doping, to observe spin-flip luminescence.
result: Observation of sharp photoluminescence associated with a triplet transition, tunable by crystal field effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the optical signatures of magnetic order in layered materials, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou

method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements on selected materials to analyze phonon dispersion and anharmonicity.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity, leading to minimum lattice thermal conductivity comparable to amorphous limits.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new route to design materials with ultralow thermal conductivity for thermoelectrics.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action for long time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to the need for many small time steps; reducing the number of steps while maintaining accuracy would greatly improve efficiency.
method: The authors propose a machine learning approach to learn the action (a quantity related to the trajectory) that allows accurate prediction of system evolution over longer time steps.
result: The method demonstrates that machine learning can effectively reduce the number of time steps needed for accurate molecular dynamics simulations.
conclusion: Learning the action enables longer time steps in molecular dynamics, offering a potential speedup for simulations of complex systems.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity, leading to Lorentz violation and late-time cosmological acceleration.
motivation: To explore the connection between emergent gravity and thermodynamics, and to derive observable consequences of Lorentz violation.
method: The authors model gravity as an emergent thermodynamic system using an Otto cycle analogy, then introduce work-producing legs to break Lorentz invariance.
result: They find that controlled Lorentz violations can produce late-time cosmic acceleration without dark energy.
conclusion: The emergent gravity framework with thermodynamic cycles offers a novel perspective on cosmology and Lorentz symmetry.

conclusion: The coherent phonon tips provide a new approach for nanoscale characterization of materials.

title: Alternative Representation Of Multichannel Rydberg Spectra: A Modified $K$-matrix And Lu-Fano Plot Applied To The Manganese Spectroscopy
authors: Justin D. Piel And Chris H. Greene

title: Th:SBO Single Crystal: A Multifunction Material For Solid-state Nuclear Optical Clocks

result: The crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable integration of nonlinear optics with a thorium-doped host.
conclusion: Th:SBO is a promising multifunctional material for solid-state nuclear optical clocks.

authors: Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, And Laura Roberts

tldr: This paper demonstrates an interferometric technique to measure vacuum magnetic birefringence, a QED effect, using an optical cavity.
motivation: Vacuum magnetic birefringence is a predicted QED effect that has not been directly observed; measuring it would test fundamental physics.
method: The authors use an optical cavity to enhance the signal and an interferometric scheme to detect the tiny birefringence induced by a magnetic field.
result: They present a proof-of-principle demonstration and sensitivity analysis, showing the technique can reach the required precision.
conclusion: The interferometric cavity technique is a viable path to measure vacuum magnetic birefringence, potentially confirming QED predictions.

method: The authors develop a symmetry-based framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with noncollinear spin configurations, likely using first-principles calculations or model Hamiltonians.
result: They demonstrate tunability and multifunctionality driven by spin chirality in these materials.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for designing high-performance spintronic devices based on weak SOC noncollinear antiferromagnets.

authors: Ece Uykur, Marcos V. Gonçalves-Faria, Sahana Rößler, Victoria A. Ginga, Marcus Schmidt, Stephan Winnerl, Manfred Helm, And Alexander A. Tsirlin

method: Combined infrared and Raman spectroscopies with high-resolution x-ray diffraction, including analysis of mechanical stress effects on Bragg peaks.
result: Mechanical stress broadens Bragg peaks, obscuring additional structural signatures; the study clarifies the phonon spectrum and symmetry properties.
conclusion: The findings resolve ambiguities in the structural and vibrational properties of α-MnTe, contributing to the understanding of altermagnetic materials.

conclusion: The method offers a new tool for designing metasurfaces with tailored resonant properties.

result: Demonstrated that strain and Debye-Waller effects can be disentangled, providing accurate temperature determination on picosecond timescales.

method: The authors develop an accelerated, mode-resolved first-principles approach to compute phonon thermal conductivity.
result: They obtain mode-resolved thermal transport properties of monolayer MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting thermal transport in 2D materials at low temperatures, relevant for nanoelectronics.

motivation: Skyrmions in altermagnets are a novel type of magnetic texture with potential applications in spintronics, but their dynamics under pinning are not well understood.
method: The authors use an atomistic model to simulate Néel skyrmions in an altermagnet with two sublattices, applying a driving force and measuring velocity and Hall angle.
result: They find that the skyrmion velocity and Hall angle are anisotropic with respect to the drive direction due to the fourfold symmetry of the altermagnet.
conclusion: The anisotropic dynamics and pinning properties could be exploited for skyrmion-based devices, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: Standard jamming models ignore diversity in cell-cell repulsion ranges; this work aims to understand how homotypic repulsion drives percolation and jamming in multitype assemblies.
method: Develops a chromatic percolation model for two-dimensional multitype particle systems with extended-range homotypic repulsion, analyzed via simulations and theoretical mapping.
result: Finds that extended-range homotypic repulsion can induce percolation of like-type particles, which correlates with mechanical jamming transitions.
conclusion: Chromatic percolation provides a framework to connect percolation and jamming in diverse biological and soft matter systems.

title: Supratransmission In Lattices With Purely Nonlinear Coupling

method: The authors summarize their previous theory and provide new computational evidence for non-universal scaling of the nonphononic vibrational density of states using simulations of model glasses.
result: They find that the scaling exponent of the nonphononic density of states is not universal and depends on the glass preparation protocol.
conclusion: Generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory captures some features but the non-universality suggests that additional physics is needed for a complete description.

motivation: Understanding how initial biases influence global consensus in deterministic majority dynamics on large random graphs.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on random regular graphs and propose a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations that lead to minority takeover.
result: They characterize the minimal bias required for a minority to achieve global agreement and demonstrate the effectiveness of the history passing algorithm in finding such configurations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of initial conditions in majority dynamics, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

authors: Junhwan Kwon And Yong-Il Shin

conclusion: Penetrable obstacles in superfluids exhibit universal vortex shedding behavior characterized by an effective diameter, extending classical fluid dynamics concepts to quantum fluids.
